---
url: /bupha/tutorials/first-run.md
---
# Tutorial: your first bupha run

Goal: push-triggered CI on a repo, end to end, in ~10 minutes.

bupha ships as tamias packages — the fleet is a `type: bupha`
bundle and the `bupha` command is a `bins[]` shim pack
(`libraries/bupha`, ADR-0006 amendment + T-012). You install the
bundle with tamias, the provider unit runs the watcher engine
through `tamias-driver-bupha host`, and GitHub pushes flow
webhook → queue → worktree → pipeline → commit status.

Prereqs: **Linux + systemd** (provider units need systemd; the
shell runner needs bash; macOS/Windows unsupported for now); git;
the `tamias` CLI; the `bupha` command pack — `tamias install
9aia:bupha@<version>` from the org registry (needs
`TAMIAS_REGISTRY_TOKEN`), or `scripts/pack.sh` + `tamias install --allow-drivers ./libraries/bupha` from a checkout — which
registers `tamias-driver-bupha` into `$TAMIAS_HOME/drivers/`
(`cargo build --release -p bupha-driver` from this repo produces
the binary by hand); a stable public URL
for the webhook — named cloudflared tunnel or a direct box; quick
tunnels are convenient but flaky. Docker only if you use the
dagger runner.

The shipped bundles live in `libraries/` — `ci-gate` (push gate
on `main`) and `docs-deploy` (push to `docs` → site deploy). This
tutorial walks `ci-gate`; swap the name for your own bundle.

1. **Secrets first** — names only in config, values in cuora
   (canonical, T-056):

   ```sh
   printf '%s' "$BUPHA_TOKEN_VALUE"   | cuora put cuora://bupha/BUPHA_TOKEN
   printf '%s' "$WEBHOOK_SECRET_VALUE" | cuora put cuora://bupha/BUPHA_WEBHOOK_SECRET
   ```

   (`BUPHA_TOKEN` is a repo-scoped PAT for statuses + hook
   management; `BUPHA_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is the HMAC secret GitHub
   signs deliveries with. Fallback when cuora isn't available:
   `~/.config/bupha/env` — the dev-mode / no-cuora leg (the
   OS-keyring leg was dropped post-T-077).)

2. `tamias install <ref>` — fetch + unpack the bundle payload
   (driver `install` is a no-op; the payload's `fleet.toml` +
   `tamias.yaml` are the config sources).

3. `tamias deploy ci-gate` — renders `bupha-watch.service` **and**
   `bupha-worker.service` (one ingress mode each — enable ONE,
   see [tamias bundles](../how-to/tamias-bundles.md)) **and**
   runs the driver's `deploy` verb: merges `fleet.toml` with the
   manifest's `provider.ingress` and writes
   `~/.config/bupha/bundles/ci-gate.toml` — the file both units'
   `tamias-driver-bupha host|worker --config …` consume.

4. `tamias driver exec ci-gate hooks register --dry-run` — print
   the webhook plan, then `… hooks register` for real (needs the
   secrets above). This wires GitHub → the bundle's public URL —
   **standalone/dev ingress** (ADR-0007); production ingress is a
   peregrin campaign listener.

5. `tamias service enable bupha-watch` — start the standalone
   watcher (`loginctl enable-linger` once for boot persistence);
   `bupha-worker` is the substrate/production alternative — see
   [distributed runners](../how-to/distributed-runners.md).

6. `tamias driver exec ci-gate health` — ping `/hook` + unit
   probe (JSON); `tamias driver exec ci-gate status` — per-unit
   is-active/is-enabled; `tamias driver exec ci-gate logs` —
   journalctl over the provider units.

7. Push. `ci/bupha` commit status appears; superseded/cancelled
   shas get honest error statuses.

Done. Logs: `journalctl --user -u bupha-watch -f` (or
`tamias driver exec ci-gate logs --lines 200`).

## Local reproduction (dev harness)

To reproduce a red run without touching the deployment, use the
dev CLI — install the command pack (`scripts/pack.sh` then
`tamias install --allow-drivers ./libraries/bupha` from this
repo), then in the repo: `bupha doctor` checks the box against a
config, `bupha run` executes the configured runner in the watched
`dir` — the same pipeline, locally. `bupha watch` runs the whole
engine standalone (no tamias, no peregrin) — the ADR-0007
fallback ingress, not the product path.

# How-to: watch multiple repos

Add one `[[repo]]` entry per repository; `name` must equal the
payload's `repository.full_name`. Each repo gets its own pending
slot; a single global worker serializes runs (deliberate — safe on
one box). Same-repo pushes may cancel their own in-flight run
(`cancel_running`); a push never cancels another repo's run.

Snippets are TOML; the equivalent `bupha.yaml`/`bupha.yml` works
identically and is preferred when both exist (TOML is permanent —
see [config reference](../reference/config.md)).

```toml
[[repo]]
name = "org/api"
dir = "/srv/checkouts/api"
queue = "all" # every push runs (releases)
secret_env = "API_WEBHOOK_SECRET" # optional per-repo hook secret

[[repo]]
name = "org/web"
dir = "/srv/checkouts/web" # default latest-wins (and the global
                           # trigger.secret_env)

# [repo.runner]                # per-repo override; replaces global
#   kind = "shell"
#   cmd = "./release.sh"
```

## Multiple pipelines on one repo — `[[repo.jobs]]`

A repo that needs more than one pipeline (a main gate plus a
docs-branch deploy, a debounced release next to the CI gate)
declares jobs instead of a second `[[repo]]` — duplicate `name`
entries are rejected at load. Each job gets its own `branch`,
`queue`, `runner` and status context; branch/queue/runner fall back
job → repo → global. Jobs share the repo's webhook, `secret_env`
and clone — one push to a ref feeds every job watching it.

```toml
[[repo]]
name = "org/app"
dir = "/srv/checkouts/app"

[[repo.jobs]]
name = "gate"                    # worktrees: <base>-org-app-gate-<sha12>
branch = "refs/heads/main"       # statuses: ci/bupha/gate
[repo.jobs.runner]
kind = "shell"
cmd = "bash scripts/ci.sh"

[[repo.jobs]]
name = "docs"
branch = "refs/heads/docs"
context = "ci/docs-deploy"       # status context override
[repo.jobs.runner]
kind = "shell"
cmd = "bash scripts/deploy-docs.sh"
```

`bupha runs org/app` (dev CLI) lists `org/app:gate` and
`org/app:docs` records; `bupha runs org/app:gate` filters to the
one job. On a deployed bundle the same data comes from the
driver's `bupha:runs` pavo view (`repo` param matches
`owner/name` and `owner/name:job` keys).

`secret_env` names an env var (resolved like `trigger.secret_env` —
env → cuora (canonical — every fleet secret migrated, T-059) → `~/.config/bupha/env` (env file = dev-mode / no-cuora fallback; keyring leg dropped post-T-077),
never the value. Each repo's
hook can then be managed and rotated independently: the watcher
resolves the target repo before verifying, so a push signed with one
repo's secret fails for every other repo — knowing the global secret
(or another team's) doesn't let a hook admin cross-forge. Repos
without `secret_env` share the global.

Standalone/dev: run `bupha deploy webhook` once — it registers
the hook on every watched repo, each with its own secret.
Bundle path: `tamias driver exec <bundle> hooks register` does
the same from `provider.ingress[].hooks[]` — **standalone/dev
ingress** per ADR-0007 (production ingress is a peregrin
campaign). `status_repo` on an entry redirects statuses (e.g.
mirror repos); it defaults to `name`.

url: /bupha/how-to/shell-runner.md
---
# How-to: run without containers

`runner.kind = "shell"` + `cmd` (alias: `"script"`) — the watcher still does webhook
verification, the queue, detached worktrees and statuses; your script
does the build. No dagger, no docker, no image pulls.

Snippets are TOML; `bupha.yaml`/`bupha.yml` is preferred and works
identically (see [config reference](../reference/config.md)).

```toml
[runner]
kind = "shell"
cmd = "./ci.sh" # run with `bash -c` in the worktree
```

The worktree is a detached checkout of the pushed sha at
`<worktree.base>-<repo>-<sha12>`, removed after the run. A killed
run reports "cancelled (superseded)", not failure.

Use it for: `make ci`, `./ci.sh`, a linter gate, or bupha's own
`scripts/release.sh` (debounced release job). For anything heavier
— cache volumes, toolchains, parallel shards — use the `dagger`
runner and the shared `modules/dagger` module.

---

---
url: /bupha/how-to/gha-runner.md
---
# How-to: run your GitHub Actions workflows on your own box

`runner.kind = "gha"` executes the repo's own
`.github/workflows/*.yml` — GitHub Actions as a bupha dialect.
Push lands on bupha's queue as usual; instead of `ci.sh` or a
dagger call, the runner parses the workflows at the pushed sha
and runs every `on.push`-matching one in one local bash
process — jobs scheduled by `needs` depth (independent jobs run
concurrently, each in its own `git worktree` checkout; `needs`
chains stay sequential), matrix legs in parallel (each in its
own `git worktree` checkout, capped by
`strategy.max-parallel`). The aggregate exit status drives the commit status.

> **Naming (T-054).** `runner.kind = "gha"` is the *workflow
> dialect* — bupha reads `.github/workflows` YAML and executes it.
> The reverse direction (bupha as a GitHub self-hosted runner that
> repos target with `runs-on: [self-hosted, bupha]`) is the
> separate `gha-runner` surface — see
> [self-hosted runner](self-hosted-runner.md). Don't confuse
> the two.

```toml
[[repo]]
name = "org/app"
dir = "/srv/checkouts/app"
branch = "refs/heads/main"

[repo.runner]
kind = "gha"
# workflow = "ci.yml"        # optional: pin file(s) under
                             # .github/workflows/ instead of
                             # discovering all on.push matches
```

The worktree is already a checkout of the pushed sha, so
`actions/checkout` is accepted as a verification no-op (any ref —
it does not re-checkout). `runs-on` labels are recorded for logs;
execution is always local — there is no runner fleet inside a
workflow.

## The supported subset — read before migrating

v1 covers the common CI shape: `on.push` (branches/paths
filters), `jobs` with `needs` (fail-fast DAG), `env`,
`defaults.run`, `steps` (`run` + `uses:` — `actions/checkout`,
`dtolnay/rust-toolchain`, `actions/setup-{node,python,go,java,
dotnet}`, `actions/upload-artifact`/`download-artifact`,
`actions/cache{,/save,/restore}`, `docker://<image>` container
steps, and composite actions via
`./local/path` or `owner/repo[/path]@ref`, with `id:`), job
`outputs:`
maps, job/step `if:` (a real expression subset — literals,
`==`/`!=`/`&&`/`||`/`!`, `contains`/`startsWith`/`endsWith`,
`success()`/`failure()`/`cancelled()`/`always()`, plus
`needs.*.result`/`steps.*.conclusion`/`steps.*.outputs.*`/
`needs.*.outputs.*`/`inputs.*`-in-composites refs),
`timeout-minutes` (GNU `timeout` per
step, process-group watchdog per job), the `$GITHUB_ENV`/
`$GITHUB_OUTPUT`/`$GITHUB_PATH`/`$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`/
`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`/`RUNNER_TEMP` file commands, and
`strategy.matrix` fan-out — legs run **in parallel** by default
(each in a private `git worktree` under the run's tmp dir, so
workspace writes stay per-leg; `max-parallel` caps concurrency,
`1` pins the sequential shared-worktree path).

Everything else is a **hard error at spawn**, naming the
unsupported key — `services:`, `container:`, `environment:`,
`concurrency:`, `continue-on-error:`, `matrix.include`/`exclude`,
`uses:` outside the list above (JS/docker
`action.yml` *definitions*, other `actions/setup-*` families and
reusable-workflow `jobs.<id>.uses:` included), `with:` keys
outside each action's declared inputs, artifact
cross-run download inputs (`run-id`,
`github-token`, `repository`, `run-attempt`),
`on.push.{tags,types,workflows}`, `secrets:`, `if:` functions
beyond the subset (`hashFiles`, `fromJSON`, `format`, …), and
unknown keys at any level (including in `action.yml`). The full
list and honest boundaries
live in `crates/bupha-gha/README.md` — treat it as the contract.

## Migrating off GHA

What you keep: the workflow files themselves, the
`on.push`/`branches`/`paths` triggers, job `needs` ordering and
`if:`/`timeout-minutes`, matrix dimensions, step
`env`/`working-directory`/`shell`, `$GITHUB_*` file commands.

What changes:

* **No marketplace — but local + composite actions work.**
  `uses:` covers `actions/checkout` (a verification no-op — the
  worktree is already at the pushed sha), `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`
  (lowers to rustup calls), the `actions/setup-*` toolchain
  family (official tarballs into a per-run toolcache), the
  artifact actions (per-run tar store, same-run only) and
  `actions/cache*` (persistent keyed store). Composite actions
  run too: `uses: ./path` reads your repo's `action.yml`, and
  `uses: owner/repo[/path]@ref` fetches the action repo over git
  (`GITHUB_TOKEN` in the runner env authenticates private repos).
  JS (`node*`) and `docker` action *definitions*, other setup
  families and reusable-workflow calls all
  hard-error — but `uses: docker://<image>` *steps* run: they
  lower to `docker run` on the host (workspace + run tmp
  bind-mounted at their paths, step/job env via `--env-file`,
  `with.entrypoint`/`with.args` supported; needs the docker CLI
  on PATH, no registry credentials or port mappings).
  `timeout-minutes` on a composite `uses:` step is a deadline
  spanning the inlined steps. Everything else installs via `run:` steps
  (`curl`, `cargo install`, your own scripts) or is already on
  the box.
* **Parallel across independent jobs, sequential across `needs`.**
  Jobs with no mutual `needs` edges share a scheduling level and
  run concurrently — each group in a private `git worktree`, like
  matrix legs (files written to the workspace stay in that
  worktree; `$BUPHA_WORKDIR`/`$BUPHA_GHA_TMP` are the shared
  channels). Levels are barriers, so a job waits for its whole
  level rather than just its needs, and there is no cross-job
  fail-fast (`strategy.fail-fast` stays per job id) — coarser
  than GHA's per-job scheduler but the same `needs` contract.
  To isolate workloads entirely, split workflows across
  `[[repo.jobs]]` entries (each gets its own `runner.workflow`
  pin and its own `ci/bupha/<job>` status context).
* **Statuses are bupha's — plus per-job detail.** The aggregate
  commit status still lands once per repo/job under `ci/bupha`
  (or your `[status].context`); on top of that, each expanded
  workflow job that reaches a verdict posts its own status under
  `<context>/<workflow>/<job id>[/<matrix bindings>]` (e.g.
  `ci/bupha/ci/build/os=ubuntu,node=18`). Skipped and
  fail-fast-cancelled legs post nothing — commit statuses have
  no neutral state.
* **Secrets** resolve the bupha way — env-var names → cuora
  (`cuora://bupha/<NAME>`, canonical; fleet secrets migrated, T-059)
  → `~/.config/bupha/env` (dev-mode / no-cuora fallback; keyring
  leg dropped post-T-077); `secrets:` context is unsupported, so
  reference ${{ env.NAME }} or plain `$NAME` in
  `run:` steps.
* **PRs are opt-in, and reuse `on.push` shapes.** The dialect
  only selects `on.push` workflows and reports
  `github.event_name = "push"` — `pull_request`-triggered
  workflows are ignored. To gate PRs, add `events = ["push",
  "pull_request"]` to the `[[repo]]`: the PR head sha runs in a
  worktree against the *base* ref's filters, so your existing
  push workflows are the PR gate too.

If a workflow hits a hard error, the run fails loudly at spawn —
the error names the key to remove or the subset to rewrite
against. For pipelines outside the subset, `runner.kind =
"shell"` + `cmd` remains the escape hatch.

## Smoke-verified subset (PL-013 D5)

Exercised end-to-end with `bupha run` (`runner.kind = "gha"`)
against a scratch repo — confirms the spawn path, not GHA/act
parity on a production workflow:

* `on.push` discovery + `steps[].run` in bash — passed.
* `uses: actions/checkout@v4` — accepted as the pushed-sha
  no-op.
* `strategy.matrix` 2×2 fan-out — 4 legs in parallel, each in its
  own worktree; ${{ matrix.node }} interpolation into `env:`
  worked.
* Unsupported key — `services:` under a job fails at spawn with
  `gha: ci.yml.jobs.<id>: unsupported key 'services' (outside the
  gha v1 subset)` — loud, names file/job/key.

## Real-repo dogfood (PL-013 D5)

`handl-lang/extension-vscode`'s `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — a
production workflow already mirrored by that repo's `ci.sh`
shell-runner gate — ran green end-to-end via `bupha run` with
`runner.kind = "gha"` (2026-11-13, scratch clone):

* `on.push.branches: [main]` discovery; `pull_request` /
  `workflow_dispatch` triggers present but not exercised by a
  local push run.
* `uses: actions/checkout@v4` no-op; `actions/setup-node@v4`
  with `node-version: "20"` resolved and `cache: npm` accepted
  as a documented no-op (no cross-run npm cache).
* `run:` steps (`npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`)
  executed in order; vitest 32/32 passed; job reported
  `gha: all jobs passed`.

Parity notes vs. GHA/act: single-job workflows in the supported
subset are drop-in. Org repos on `oven-sh/setup-bun` or
`Swatinem/rust-cache`/`astral-sh/setup-uv` are **not** yet —
those `uses:` hard-error at spawn today (the honest-failure
contract; add the action to the subset or keep `kind = "shell"`).

A full parity pass against GHA/act output is still open — the
dialect's hard-error contract means a migration is incremental:
unsupported keys surface one at a time.

url: /bupha/how-to/self-hosted-runner.md
---
# How-to: bupha as a GitHub self-hosted runner

The reverse of the [`gha` dialect](gha-runner.md): instead of
bupha *reading* `.github/workflows`, this mode makes bupha a
runner that **GitHub drives** — the crate speaks enough of the
actions/runner broker protocol (registration → session → message
queue → job offer → result report) that a workflow can say
`runs-on: [self-hosted, bupha]` and GitHub schedules the job onto
the box. `bupha` is always in the runner's label set.

> **Naming (T-054/T-065).** `runner.kind = "gha"` is the workflow
> *dialect* (bupha executes workflow YAML itself); `gha-runner` is
> the *broker protocol* (GitHub's service drives bupha). Two
> different products — keep them distinct.

This is a **dev-CLI surface** today: `bupha gha-runner <FILE>`
(the `bins[]` shim carries it like `watch`/`agent`), not a
driver verb — wrap it in your own `provider.services[]` entry or
run it standalone for now.

## Configure

The runner uses its **own** config file (TOML, serde — secrets
are env-var *names*, never values), not `bupha.yaml`:

```toml
repo = "owner/repo"                    # or an https URL; required once
name = "bupha-builder-1"               # runner list label (default bupha-<host>-<pid>)
labels = ["linux", "x64"]              # extra labels on top of self-hosted/OS/arch/bupha
instance = "github.com"                # or a GHES host
token_env = "BUPHA_GHA_RUNNER_TOKEN"   # registration token env NAME (settings UI / config.sh token)
pat_env = "GITHUB_PAT"                 # optional: PAT that mints a registration token instead
credentials = ".bupha-gha-runner.credentials.json"  # persisted after first registration
workdir = ".bupha-gha-runner-work"     # per-job workspaces
max_parallelism = 1                    # informational — one job at a time today
```

Registration is one-shot: the first run trades a registration
token (from `token_env`, a `pat_env`-minted one, or
`token_file`) for credentials persisted in `credentials` —
subsequent runs reuse them. Point a repo at the runner with a
workflow job:

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, bupha]
    steps:
      - run: echo hello
```

## Protocol coverage

Implemented: registration (incl. PAT-minted tokens and
`Default` pool lookup), session key unwrap (RSA-OAEP + AES-256),
long-poll message queue + ack, broker migration, job offers via
`acquirejob`, script steps via the job's shell, `actions/checkout`
via git, `$GITHUB_ENV`/`$GITHUB_OUTPUT`/`$GITHUB_PATH` env files,
`success()`/`failure()`/`cancelled()`/`always()` conditions, job
lease renewal, cancellation, and `completejob` with the evaluated
job `outputs:` map. Log upload uses the signed-URL append-blob
path.

Explicitly out of scope (fail loudly): node/docker actions other
than `actions/checkout`, container/service jobs, `${{ }}`
expression evaluation inside step fields (the service
pre-compiles them), the realtime websocket log feed, and
artifact/cache/upload endpoints. Full boundary:
`crates/bupha-gha-runner/src/lib.rs` module docs.

## GitHub Enterprise Server

`instance = "<ghes-host>"` (or an explicit `api_base`) points the
REST calls at `{host}/api/v3`; the broker/session endpoints come
from the tenant response, so they follow the instance
automatically. The `_apis/distributedtask` `api-version` strings
in `client.rs` are the github.com values (`6.0-preview.1` pools,
`6.0-preview.2` agents, `5.1-preview` sessions/messages) — verified
against the actions/runner protocol surface but **not yet
exercised against a live GHES**, whose pipelines service may pin
different versions. First GHES run: watch for 4xx on the session
calls; the fix is a one-line constant change per endpoint.

url: /bupha/how-to/distributed-runners.md
---
# Distributed runners

One watcher process runs CI on one box — deployed as a tamias
bundle, the provider unit execs `tamias-driver-bupha host`, which
runs this same engine in-process. Two optional pieces scale it
out; single-box behavior is unchanged when they're absent:

* the **ci-job entity plane** (P-002) — the distributed queue:
  jobs are `kind="ci-job"` entities on a hypha/peregrin node, and
  worker boxes claim them with `tamias-driver-bupha worker`;
* **`bupha agent`** + `kind = "http"` runner — a remote executor
  for boxes that can't (or shouldn't) pull.

> **Surface note (ADR-0006/0007).** `tamias-driver-bupha worker`
> is the product path for fleet workers — declare it as a second
> `provider.services[]` entry in the bundle's `tamias.yaml`
> (`bupha-worker.service`; `libraries/ci-gate` does). The dev CLI
> has no `worker` verb — the redis pull queue it used
> (`[queue] kind = "redis"`, `bupha worker`, the `bupha-queue-*`
> impl crates) was retired in T-049/T-068; `[queue]` keeps only
> the dev `json` store that backs `host`/`watch` restarts.

## The ci-job entity plane

The plane (`bupha-plane`, a hypha `EntityPlane` impl) lives **on
the node**, not in bupha: peregrin-node hosts `CiJobPlane` behind
its default-on `bupha` cargo feature (T-061). Jobs are entities
with deterministic ids `ci:{key}:{sha}:{attempt}` — replays dedup
for free — and `ci.*` ops (`enqueue`/`claim`/`renew`/`release`/
`complete`/`cancel`/`status`) carry the queue semantics
(latest-wins/FIFO, fence + lease claims) that `bupha-core`
defines.

**Ingress.** Production webhook/forge ingress is a peregrin
campaign listener (ADR-0007): it normalizes deliveries through
bupha's `Trigger` semantics and creates `ci-job` entities via
`ci.enqueue` — the `ci-ingress` campaign (T-063) does this
against `${config.node_url}/api/entities` today. The standalone
`host` watcher's local queue remains the dev/single-box path:
a job whose `runs_on` labels the box's `[worker] labels` can't
satisfy is skipped locally — it belongs to the plane's fleet.

**Workers.** `tamias-driver-bupha worker --config ~/.config/bupha/bundles/<name>.toml` polls the node
(`[worker] node` in the config, `--node` / `BUPHA_WORKER_NODE`
override), claims pending jobs this box's `[worker] labels`
cover, runs each through the same worktree → runner → status
pipeline `host` uses, renews the lease mid-run
(`BUPHA_ENTITY_LEASE_SECS`, default 300s), and settles with
`ci.complete` — which emits `ci.job.completed` to the node's
event ingest. Claim loss (a fence mismatch → 409) abandons the
run; a dead worker's job returns to `pending` when its lease
expires. Node credential: `[worker] node_token_env` names a
secret resolved through the usual chain (env → cuora →
env file) — `peregrin pair`/`hypha pair` mints the token.

```toml
[worker]
node = "http://127.0.0.1:18787"      # hypha/peregrin node base URL
node_token_env = "PEREGRIN_TOKEN"   # secret NAME, never the value
labels = ["arch=arm64"]             # this box's claim labels
# events_url = "http://127.0.0.1:29173/api/events/inject"
#   ^ optional: where ci.job.completed POSTs. Default is
#   {node}/api/events/inject — the entity node's ingest, which
#   reaches kind="campaign" entities. Campaigns hosted by
#   `peregrin campaign serve` instead need its shared listener's
#   /api/events/inject (same PEREGRIN_TOKEN bearer).
```

**Fork-PR checkout.** A `pull_request` ci-job may carry optional
`cloneUrl`/`headRef` indexDoc fields — the head repo's clone URL and
head ref, set by ci-ingress only for fork deliveries. When the job's
sha isn't already in `repo.dir`, the worker fetches
`git fetch <cloneUrl> <headRef>` (then the bare sha — forges
allowing reachable-sha wants resolve it even after the head branch
is gone), then a bare-sha fetch from `origin` (GitHub serves PR
heads, forks included, under `refs/pull/*` on the base repo), and
only then the usual remote `sync`. Pushes and same-repo PRs leave
both fields absent and keep the single-remote path. Both fields are
argv-validated at the plane's trust boundary (`is_safe_remote` /
`is_safe_ref_name` — no option injection, no `ext::` transport
escapes, no refspec writes).

**Private forks.** A fork of a private repo is itself private — an
unauthenticated `git fetch https://github.com/<fork>.git` fails.
Fork fetches ride the same git credential machinery as `origin`
(global credential helpers, `url.insteadOf`, `gh auth setup-git`),
so a box whose origin auth already covers the fork host often needs
nothing. When it doesn't, `[worker] fork_token_env` names a secret
holding a git credential (PAT):

```toml
[worker]
fork_token_env = "BUPHA_FORK_GIT_TOKEN"   # secret NAME, never the value
```

The NAME resolves through the usual chain (env → cuora
`cuora://bupha/<NAME>` → `~/.config/bupha/env`). The worker
materializes a git credential-helper script under the config dir
that re-resolves the NAME at fetch time — the value never enters
bupha's argv, the worker's env, the repo config, or the CI job's
environment, and the helper is attached via `-c
credential.helper=` only for the fork fetch. A fine-grained PAT
that reads both the base org and the fork works as-is; fork creds
that differ from origin creds get their own NAME. `username` is
sent as `x-access-token` (the GitHub PAT convention). With the knob
absent, or when the secret doesn't resolve, the fetch falls through
to the unauthenticated path and the job fails after the remote
fallbacks — `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` keeps a private fork from ever
blocking on a credential prompt.

## Label routing (multi-arch)

`runs_on` on a `[[repo]]`/`[[repo.jobs]]` entry becomes the
entity's `runsOn` at fleet normalization (T-067): a job runs only
on workers whose `[worker] labels` satisfy every requirement.
Unlabeled jobs are claimable by anyone.

```toml
# ingress/fleet spec
[[repo]]
name = "org/firmware"
dir = "/srv/repos/firmware"
runs_on = ["arch=arm64"]

# on the ARM worker box
[worker]
labels = ["arch=arm64"]
node = "http://peregrin-node:18787"
node_token_env = "PEREGRIN_TOKEN"
```

This is per-repo arch pinning; a same-push multi-arch *matrix*
(one sha → N parallel arch runs) is future work. A standalone
`host` watcher applies the same rule locally — it only enqueues
jobs its own `[worker] labels` cover, so labeled work always
lands on the plane, never on the wrong box.

## Remote agent + http runner

For a box you drive explicitly (it doesn't pull from the plane):

```toml
# on the CI box
[runner]
kind = "http"
agent_url = "http://arm-box:29174"
secret_env = "BUPHA_AGENT_SECRET"   # env NAME — value never in config

# on the remote box
[agent]
listen = "0.0.0.0:29174"
token_env = "BUPHA_AGENT_SECRET"
[runner]
kind = "script"
cmd = "bash ci.sh"
```

The runner POSTs `{key, sha, cmd, env names}` to `/jobs`, PUTs the
tarred worktree to `/jobs/{id}/worktree`, polls `GET /jobs/{id}`,
and `DELETE`s to kill. Every request carries
`X-Bupha-Auth: sha256=<hmac(body)>` verified against the shared
secret. `bupha agent` is a dev-CLI surface (the `bins[]` shim
carries it); for a deployed unit wrap it in your own
`provider.services[]` entry or run it standalone. Caveats mirror
the ssh runner: remote kills are best-effort and tarred `.git`
pointer files are broken on the agent.

# How-to: use bupha as a GitHub Action

`uses: 9aia/bupha` is a composite action at the bupha repo root —
bash + curl/jq only, no build step and **no bupha listener needed**.
It reads the forge's combined commit-status API, which is where
bupha's watcher posts its verdicts (`[status].context`, default
`ci/bupha`).

Typical use: a repo's own GHA workflow waits for — or reports — the
bupha gate verdict on a sha, without checking out anything or
reaching the bupha box.

## Gate on the bupha verdict

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  statuses: read          # required for private repos

jobs:
  bupha-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: 9aia/bupha@main    # pin to a tag or SHA in production
        with:
          mode: wait
          timeout: "900"
```

`mode: wait` polls
`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/status`, picks the latest
entry matching `context` (default `ci/bupha`), and exits non-zero
when the status reaches `failure`, `error`, or the timeout elapses —
the step is a drop-in required check.

## Report the verdict without failing

```yaml
- uses: 9aia/bupha@main
  id: bupha
  with:
    mode: status            # one fetch, always exit 0
- run: echo "bupha: ${{ steps.bupha.outputs.state }} — ${{ steps.bupha.outputs.description }}"
```

Outputs:

| output | values |
| ------ | ------ |
| `state` | `pending` `success` `failure` `error` `none` `timeout` |
| `description` | the status description bupha posted |
| `target-url` | status `target_url` (run/log link) |

`none` means nothing was posted for that sha/context yet — usually
the webhook hasn't landed or the repo isn't watched. In `wait` mode
`none` is treated as not-terminal and keeps polling.

## Inputs

| input | default | notes |
| ----- | ------- | ----- |
| `mode` | `wait` | `status` (one shot) or `wait` (poll to terminal) |
| `sha` | ${{ github.sha }} | for `pull_request`, prefer `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` |
| `context` | `ci/bupha` | must match the bundle's `[status].context` |
| `repo` | ${{ github.repository }} | `owner/repo` |
| `token` | ${{ github.token }} | needs `statuses: read` on private repos |
| `api-base` | `https://api.github.com` | GHES override |
| `timeout` | `600` | seconds, wait mode; integer `0`–`86400` |
| `interval` | `15` | seconds between polls; integer `>= 1` |

Both knobs are validated up front (exit 2 on a bad value) — a
non-numeric or out-of-range input fails fast instead of dying
mid-poll. In `wait` mode a failed fetch or unparseable response
is treated as transient and retried until the deadline; in
`status` mode it exits 1 with a clean error.

## What it does *not* do

There is no `trigger` mode. Firing a bupha run from GHA would mean a
public, unauthenticated ingress — production webhook/forge ingress is
peregrin-owned and the bupha webhook listener requires an HMAC
signature (ADR-0007). To kick CI off, push to a watched ref, use the
bundle's `hooks register`, or drive a peregrin campaign.

## Manual test

No live GitHub needed — stub `curl` and exercise the script:

```sh
mkdir /tmp/fake && cat > /tmp/fake/curl <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cat <<'JSON'
{"state":"success","statuses":[
 {"context":"ci/bupha","state":"success","description":"ci passed",
  "target_url":"https://example/run/1","created_at":"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]}
JSON
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/fake/curl
PATH=/tmp/fake:$PATH BUPHA_MODE=status BUPHA_SHA=abc BUPHA_REPO=o/r \
  GITHUB_OUTPUT=/tmp/out.txt \
  bash scripts/gha-status.sh && cat /tmp/out.txt
```

# How-to: package bupha fleets with tamias

A bupha fleet — watcher unit + operator config + webhook wiring —
ships as a tamias content bundle (`type: bupha`). tamias owns the
package lifecycle (fetch, install store, provider units, hooks);
bupha owns what runs inside. The shipped examples live in
`libraries/`: `ci-gate` (push-to-verdict gate on `main`),
`docs-deploy` (push to `docs` → site deploy → `docs/deploy`
status), and `ci-ingress` — a `peregrin-bundle`, not `type: bupha`:
the forge webhook → `ci-job` entity campaign that feeds the worker
fleet (CI orchestration knowledge lives here even though the bundle
type is peregrin's).

## The `type: bupha` contract

Two files make a bundle:

* **`tamias.yaml`** — the package manifest. `provider:` declares
  the systemd unit(s) (`<provider.name>-<service>`), the env file,
  and `ingress[]` — the public URL, listen address, and the
  GitHub hooks to manage. `verbs:` is advisory for
  `tamias provider list`/`tamias run`.
* **`fleet.toml`** — a *complete* `bupha_core::Config` doc: the
  `[[repo]]` set plus `[runner]`/`[status]`/`[queue]`/`[worktree]`
  blocks, and optionally `[worker] node`/`node_token_env` for the
  entity-plane worker. `tamias-driver-bupha deploy` merges the
  manifest-owned fields (`tunnel.public_url`, `trigger.listen`,
  `trigger.kind`) into it and writes
  `~/.config/bupha/bundles/<name>.toml` — the config BOTH provider
  verbs consume: `host --config` (the watcher) and
  `worker --config` (the ci-job consumer).

A bundle declares **two services, one per ingress mode**
(ADR-0007): `watch`/`watch-docs` runs `tamias-driver-bupha host`
— the standalone/dev watcher behind `provider.ingress`'s webhook
listener — and `worker`/`worker-docs` runs
`tamias-driver-bupha worker` — the substrate/production consumer
(P-002) that polls `kind="ci-job"` entities on the hypha/peregrin
node named by `[worker] node`. Enable ONE: both at once would
fight over the listener port and double-run pushes.

Secrets are env-var **names** everywhere (`secret_env`,
`token_env`); values resolve env → **cuora**
(`cuora://bupha/<NAME>` via the `cuora` CLI — canonical, T-056;
every fleet secret migrated there in T-059) → `~/.config/bupha/env`
(the dev-mode / no-cuora fallback — the OS-keyring leg was
dropped post-T-077; the file is retired and no unit sets
`EnvironmentFile`). Seed/rotate with
`printf '%s' "$VALUE" | cuora put cuora://bupha/<NAME>`.
Never a value in either file.

> **Ingress note (ADR-0007).** The `provider.ingress` block +
> `hooks register` wire the bupha webhook listener — the
> **standalone/dev** ingress for deployments with no peregrin.
> Production webhook/forge ingress is a peregrin campaign
> listener that normalizes deliveries through bupha's `Trigger`
> semantics and enqueues `ci-job` via `ci.enqueue` — consumed by
> the bundle's `worker` service, not its `watch` service.

## Install → deploy → hooks

```sh
tamias install <ref>            # fetch + unpack; driver install is a no-op
tamias deploy <bundle>          # render the provider unit AND write
                                # bundles/<name>.toml from fleet.toml + ingress
tamias driver exec <bundle> hooks register --dry-run   # webhook plan
tamias driver exec <bundle> hooks register             # upsert GitHub hooks
tamias service enable <unit>   # start the watcher (e.g. bupha-watch-docs)
tamias uninstall <bundle>      # remove unit + bundles/<name>.toml
```

`tamias driver exec <bundle>` verbs: `hooks register`
(create/update the declared forge hooks), `health` (ping `/hook`

* unit probe, JSON), `status` (per-unit is-active/is-enabled),
  `logs` (journalctl over the provider units). `tamias driver
  config-schema <bundle>` prints the JSON Schema of the operator
  config `deploy` writes.

The driver — `tamias-driver-bupha`, built from
`crates/bupha-driver` — is dual-surface: the tamias verbs above
plus the pavo view verbs (`manifest`/`capabilities`/`serve`)
that serve bupha's read-only CI views. tamias finds it on `PATH`
or in `$TAMIAS_HOME/drivers/`.

## Writing your own bundle

1. Copy `libraries/docs-deploy/` — it's the smaller template.
2. Edit `fleet.toml`: one `[[repo]]` per watched repo
   (`name`/`dir`/`branch`; `events = ["push", "pull_request"]`
   opts into PR deliveries), the `[runner]` your pipelines need
   (`shell` + `cmd`, `gha` + `workflow`, `dagger`, …), and
   `[status].context` for the commit-status label.
3. Edit `tamias.yaml`: `provider.services[]` execs should be
   `tamias-driver-bupha host --config ~/.config/bupha/bundles/<name>.toml`
   for the watcher and `tamias-driver-bupha worker --config ~/.config/bupha/bundles/<name>.toml` for the entity-plane
   consumer (the driver binary from `$TAMIAS_HOME/drivers/` or
   `PATH` — both verbs run the engine in-process);
   pick **unique service names** — the unit is
   `<provider.name>-<service>`, and two bundles sharing
   `bupha-watch.service`/`bupha-worker.service` would overwrite
   each other (ci-gate owns `watch`+`worker`, docs-deploy owns
   `watch-docs`+`worker-docs`). Give `ingress[]` a
   distinct `listen` port and `public_url`, and one `hooks[]`
   entry per `[[repo]]`. A substrate-mode bundle still declares
   `ingress[]` (it's the standalone fallback + the source of
   `tunnel.public_url`/`trigger.listen` in the generated config)
   but only enables the worker unit.
4. `bupha runs --config fleet.toml` (dev CLI) smoke-checks the
   payload parses as a `Config` before you publish.

Two watchers can watch the same repo: GitHub delivers every push
to both hook URLs and each fleet's `branch` filter keeps only its
own refs — `main` for the gate, `docs` for deploys. Overlap costs
a filtered delivery, not a double run.

Coming from a peregrin campaign instead? The dev CLI's
`bupha import <campaign.yaml>` translates the github-webhook +
git-job + github-status shape into a `bupha.yaml` fleet config —
a head start for the `fleet.toml` inside step 2.

# How-to: sccache backend

sccache's backend is decoupled via an env file — set
`[cache] conf` to a `KEY=VAL` file (mounted into containers as
a secret). Without it, sccache uses a local cache volume.

## Local S3 (garage)

```
DATA=${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/bupha

docker run -d --name garage --restart always \
  -v $DATA/garage:/data \
  -v $DATA/garage.toml:/etc/garage.toml \
  -p 9100:9100 dxflrs/garage:v1.x.x
```

Then in the garage CLI: `bucket create bupha-ci` → `key create sccache`
→ `bucket allow --read --write --owner bupha-ci --key sccache`.

Env file:

```
SCCACHE_ENDPOINT=http://<docker-gateway>:9100
SCCACHE_BUCKET=bupha-ci
SCCACHE_REGION=garage
SCCACHE_S3_USE_SSL=false
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
```

## Migrating to hosted S3 (R2 / AWS)

Same file, new values — `SCCACHE_ENDPOINT` to the provider URL, real
region, new creds. No code changes; that's the point of the env file.

# Command-Line Help for `bupha`

This document contains the help content for the `bupha` command-line program.

the oxpecker on your repo's back — headless CI

**Command Overview:**

* [`bupha`↴](#bupha)
* [`bupha watch`↴](#bupha-watch)
* [`bupha agent`↴](#bupha-agent)
* [`bupha gha-runner`↴](#bupha-gha-runner)
* [`bupha init`↴](#bupha-init)
* [`bupha doctor`↴](#bupha-doctor)
* [`bupha run`↴](#bupha-run)
* [`bupha deploy`↴](#bupha-deploy)
* [`bupha deploy service`↴](#bupha-deploy-service)
* [`bupha deploy webhook`↴](#bupha-deploy-webhook)
* [`bupha deploy env`↴](#bupha-deploy-env)
* [`bupha deploy check`↴](#bupha-deploy-check)
* [`bupha deploy release`↴](#bupha-deploy-release)
* [`bupha destroy`↴](#bupha-destroy)
* [`bupha destroy service`↴](#bupha-destroy-service)
* [`bupha destroy webhook`↴](#bupha-destroy-webhook)
* [`bupha destroy worktrees`↴](#bupha-destroy-worktrees)
* [`bupha service`↴](#bupha-service)
* [`bupha service enable`↴](#bupha-service-enable)
* [`bupha service disable`↴](#bupha-service-disable)
* [`bupha service status`↴](#bupha-service-status)
* [`bupha service restart`↴](#bupha-service-restart)
* [`bupha service logs`↴](#bupha-service-logs)
* [`bupha runs`↴](#bupha-runs)
* [`bupha log`↴](#bupha-log)
* [`bupha explain`↴](#bupha-explain)
* [`bupha import`↴](#bupha-import)

## `bupha`

the oxpecker on your repo's back — headless CI

**Usage:** `bupha [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `watch` — Serve the source → queue → runner loop (forge webhook, sturn WAL poller — every configured source)
* `agent` — Serve the remote-run agent — accepts jobs from `kind="http"` runners and executes them with this box's \[runner]
* `gha-runner` — Serve as a GitHub Actions self-hosted runner — registers with a repo (once), then polls GitHub's broker protocol and runs the jobs it is offered (`runs-on: [self-hosted, bupha]`). Uses bupha-gha-runner's own config file, not bupha.yaml
* `init` — Scaffold dagger CI in a repo (dagger init, pinned module, delegate template) and converge its AGENTS.md to the managed agent-awareness block. For the script runner, a ci.sh is enough
* `doctor` — Check what the loaded config actually needs on this box
* `run` — Run the pipeline locally — in the watched repo's `dir`, not cwd
* `deploy` — Install-time helpers — no manual file copies
* `destroy` — Teardown counterparts of `deploy`
* `service` — Toggle the watcher unit without removing it — free the box when CI isn't needed, `enable` brings it back
* `runs` — Recent finished runs (reads `<worktree.base>/history.jsonl`)
* `log` — Raw run log — last N lines of history.jsonl
* `explain` — Why a sha did/didn't run — history + queue + worktree state
* `import` — Translate a peregrin campaign YAML (ci-gate fleet shape) into a bupha.yaml — no config file needed

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha watch`

Serve the source → queue → runner loop (forge webhook, sturn WAL poller — every configured source)

**Usage:** `bupha watch [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha agent`

Serve the remote-run agent — accepts jobs from `kind="http"` runners and executes them with this box's \[runner]

**Usage:** `bupha agent [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha gha-runner`

Serve as a GitHub Actions self-hosted runner — registers with a repo (once), then polls GitHub's broker protocol and runs the jobs it is offered (`runs-on: [self-hosted, bupha]`). Uses bupha-gha-runner's own config file, not bupha.yaml

**Usage:** `bupha gha-runner [OPTIONS] <FILE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<FILE>` — Runner config file (TOML — bupha-gha-runner::Config). Positional: `--config` is already the global bupha.yaml flag, and clap arg ids must stay unique per command

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha init`

Scaffold dagger CI in a repo (dagger init, pinned module, delegate template) and converge its AGENTS.md to the managed agent-awareness block. For the script runner, a ci.sh is enough

**Usage:** `bupha init [OPTIONS] [DIR]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `[DIR]` — Repo dir to initialize (default: cwd) \[default: .]

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha doctor`

Check what the loaded config actually needs on this box

**Usage:** `bupha doctor [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `--json` — Machine-readable JSON output — `{"ok", "failures", "checks"}`
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha run`

Run the pipeline locally — in the watched repo's `dir`, not cwd

**Usage:** `bupha run [OPTIONS] [FUNCTION]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `[FUNCTION]` — Function for the dagger runner (default: from config)

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha deploy`

Install-time helpers — no manual file copies

**Usage:** `bupha deploy [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `service` — Write + enable the systemd user unit (needs enable-linger for boot persistence)
* `webhook` — Register/update the repo's push webhook via the REST API (token resolved env → cuora → env file — no `gh` dependency)
* `env` — Seed ~/.config/bupha/env with the secret names
* `check` — Verify the whole install: unit, secrets, hook, endpoint, token
* `release` — Tag the workspace version `{repo}-v{ver}` and push it. crates.io publish is retired — releases ride the tamias pack

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha deploy service`

Write + enable the systemd user unit (needs enable-linger for boot persistence)

**Usage:** `bupha deploy service [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `--no-start` — Skip enable --now (write the file only)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha deploy webhook`

Register/update the repo's push webhook via the REST API (token resolved env → cuora → env file — no `gh` dependency)

**Usage:** `bupha deploy webhook [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

Verify the whole install: unit, secrets, hook, endpoint, token

###### **Options:**

Tag the workspace version `{repo}-v{ver}` and push it. crates.io publish is retired — releases ride the tamias pack

## `bupha destroy`

Teardown counterparts of `deploy`

**Usage:** `bupha destroy [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `service` — Disable + remove the systemd user unit
* `webhook` — Delete the repo's webhook whose URL matches tunnel.public_url
* `worktrees` — Remove detached worktrees and the persisted queue file

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha destroy service`

Disable + remove the systemd user unit

**Usage:** `bupha destroy service [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha destroy webhook`

Delete the repo's webhook whose URL matches tunnel.public_url

**Usage:** `bupha destroy webhook [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha destroy worktrees`

Remove detached worktrees and the persisted queue file

**Usage:** `bupha destroy worktrees [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha service`

Toggle the watcher unit without removing it — free the box when CI isn't needed, `enable` brings it back

**Usage:** `bupha service [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `enable` — Enable + start the watcher unit now and at login
* `disable` — Stop the watcher now; stays stopped across logins until `service enable` (the unit file is kept)
* `status` — Whether the watcher unit is enabled and running
* `restart` — Restart the watcher unit
* `logs` — Print (or follow, -f) the watcher unit log

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha service enable`

Enable + start the watcher unit now and at login

**Usage:** `bupha service enable [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha service disable`

Stop the watcher now; stays stopped across logins until `service enable` (the unit file is kept)

**Usage:** `bupha service disable [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha service status`

Whether the watcher unit is enabled and running

**Usage:** `bupha service status [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha service restart`

Restart the watcher unit

**Usage:** `bupha service restart [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha service logs`

Print (or follow, -f) the watcher unit log

**Usage:** `bupha service logs [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-f, --f` — Follow the log stream (journalctl -f)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha runs`

Recent finished runs (reads `<worktree.base>/history.jsonl`)

**Usage:** `bupha runs [OPTIONS] [REPO]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `[REPO]` — Filter to one repo ("owner/name")

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha log`

Raw run log — last N lines of history.jsonl

**Usage:** `bupha log [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-n, --n <N>` — Lines to show \[default: 50]
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha explain`

Why a sha did/didn't run — history + queue + worktree state

**Usage:** `bupha explain [OPTIONS] <SHA>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<SHA>` — The pushed sha (any prefix ≥ 4 chars)

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `bupha import`

Translate a peregrin campaign YAML (ci-gate fleet shape) into a bupha.yaml — no config file needed

**Usage:** `bupha import [OPTIONS] <FILE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<FILE>` — Campaign file (e.g. libraries/ci-gate/main.yaml)

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Path to the config file — bupha.yaml/.yml or bupha.toml (default: ./bupha.\* or ~/.config/bupha/, YAML preferred)
* `--out <OUT>` — Write the generated config here instead of stdout
* `--dir <OWNER/REPO=PATH>` — Clone-path override `owner/name=/path` (repeatable) — wins over cmd-derived and default dirs
* `--pull-request` — Also run every repo on pull_request deliveries (`events: [push, pull_request]`)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

# Config — `bupha.yaml` / `bupha.toml`

Both formats are permanent. `bupha.yaml`/`.yml` are preferred
over `bupha.toml` at each search step — `--config`,
`$BUPHA_CONFIG`, `./bupha.*`, `~/.config/bupha/bupha.*` — and an
explicit `.toml` path still parses as TOML. Fields below are
spelled in TOML; in YAML the same names nest under `:` maps
(`[[repo]]` → `repos:`/`repo:` list, `[repo.runner]` → `runner:`
map). Local-path fields (`dir`, `base`, `sccache_conf`,
`cli_source`, `audit.path`, `telemetry.path`, `attest.dir`,
`cache.conf`) expand a leading `~/` to `$HOME` at load in both
formats. See `examples/bupha.toml.example` and
`examples/bupha.yaml.example`.

In a deployed tamias bundle this file is generated by
`tamias-driver-bupha deploy` (`fleet.toml` + `provider.ingress`
→ `~/.config/bupha/bundles/<name>.toml`) and consumed by the
driver's `host` and `worker` verbs — watcher engine and
ci-job entity consumer. The `bupha` CLI's
`--config`/`doctor` verbs are the dev-harness path (ADR-0006:
no user-facing CLI).

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repos` | `Vec<RepoEntry>` | required | Watched repos — each expands to one pending slot per job (one implicit job when `[[repo.jobs]]` is absent), all fed by one global worker. TOML-conventional singular; `repos` kept as alias for existing configs. |
| `trigger` | `TriggerCfg` | optional | Optional — entity worker boxes never listen. |
| `tunnel` | `TunnelCfg` | optional | How the listener is exposed publicly (cloudflared, direct, none). |
| `cache` | `CacheCfg` | optional | Artifact cache backend (`[cache]`); `runner.sccache_conf` is accepted for older configs — `[cache]` wins. |
| `access` | `AccessCfg` | optional | Who may trigger (`[access]`). Absent = open. |
| `audit` | `AuditCfg` | optional | Decision/outcome audit log (`[audit]`). Absent = none. |
| `telemetry` | `TelemetryCfg` | optional | Pipeline observability (`[telemetry]`). Absent = none. |
| `attest` | `AttestCfg` | optional | Run provenance (`[attest]`). Absent = none. |
| `queue` | `QueueCfg` | optional | Dev queue persistence backend (`[queue]`). Absent = json. |
| `worker` | `WorkerCfg` | optional | Entity-plane worker endpoint + fleet routing labels (`[worker]`) — `node`/`node_token_env` for the ci-job consumer, `labels` for queue-job filtering. Absent = defaults (no node, no labels). |
| `agent` | `AgentCfg` | optional | Remote-run agent (`[agent]`). Absent = no agent listener. |
| `worktree` | `WorktreeCfg` | optional | Where detached git worktrees for runs are created. |

## `[[repo]]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | required | repository.full_name in the webhook payload ("owner/name") — also the status target repo. |
| `dir` | `path` | required | Clone to fetch + create detached worktrees from. A leading `~/` expands to `$HOME` at load. |
| `branch` | `string` | optional | The ref to watch (e.g. "refs/heads/main"). |
| `status_repo` | `string` | optional | Status repo override (defaults to `name`). |
| `runner` | `RunnerCfg` | optional | Per-repo runner override — a full \[repo.runner] table replaces the global `[runner]` for this repo. |
| `queue` | `"latest" | "all"` | optional | Queue policy — `latest` (default) or `all` (run every push). |
| `secret_env` | `string` | optional | Per-repo webhook-secret env var — a NAME resolved like `trigger.secret_env` (its fallback). Lets each repo's hook be managed and rotated independently of the other watched repos. |
| `runs_on` | `list` | optional | Fleet routing: labels a claiming worker must carry (e.g. \["arch=arm64"]). Empty = any worker. Per-repo arch pinning — same-push multi-arch matrix is future work. |
| `retry` | `u32` | optional | Failed runs re-enqueue at the back this many times (0..3, ADR-0002 §3). 0 = today's behavior. A *failed* sha may retry — a superseded or claim-lost one may not. |
| `sturn` | `bool` | optional | Opt this repo into the `[trigger.sturn]` WAL poller — its jobs enqueue on `Op::Snapshot` events found under `refs/sturn/wal/*` in `dir`, no webhook needed. Repo-level: every job inherits it (branch filters still apply). |
| `events` | `list` | optional | Source event kinds this repo runs on — "push" and/or "pull_request" (GitHub webhook deliveries). Empty = \["push"] (today's behavior). Repo-level: every job inherits it. |
| `jobs` | `Vec<JobEntry>` | optional | Pipelines within this repo (`[[repo.jobs]]`). Each job gets its own branch filter, queue policy, runner and status context — one webhook feeds them all. Empty = the repo itself is its single implicit pipeline. |

## `[trigger]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api_base` | `string` | optional | Forge API base — GHES ("https://ghe.acme/api/v3") or default github.com. Used by the trigger, status, and forge-admin impls. |
| `kind` | `string` | optional | "github" today; other forges = new impl crates. Empty is valid only when \[trigger.sturn] supplies the pushes — a sturn-only watcher needs no listener or webhook secret. |
| `sturn` | `SturnTriggerCfg` | optional | Optional sturn-native push source — see SturnTriggerCfg. |
| `listen` | `string` | optional | Webhook listener bind address ("127.0.0.1:29173"). |
| `secret_env` | `string` | optional | Env var holding the webhook secret — the default for every watched repo; `[[repo]] secret_env` overrides it per repo. |

## `[runner]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `string` | required | Runner kind: "dagger" | "shell" | "ssh" | impl crates. |
| `token_env` | `string` | optional | Env var name holding the forge token (never the value). |
| `cancel_running` | `bool` | optional | Kill an in-flight run when a newer push supersedes it. Invalid with `queue = "all"` (rejected at load). |
| `extra` | `toml::Table` | required | Impl-owned fields — the matched impl crate deserializes its own config struct from this; core knows none of them. |

## `[status]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `string` | optional | "github" | "log" (stdout only) | "none". |
| `repo` | `string` | optional | owner/repo for the commit-status API. |
| `context` | `string` | optional | Status context label (e.g. "ci/bupha"). |

## `[tunnel]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `string` | optional | "none" | "cloudflared" | "direct". |
| `name` | `string` | optional | Named tunnel (stable URL); empty = quick tunnel. |
| `local_url` | `string` | optional | Local URL the tunnel forwards to (listener address). |
| `public_url` | `string` | optional | provider=direct: the external URL GitHub should hit. |

## `[cache]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `string` | optional | Backend id ("sccache"; "none"/empty disables). |
| `conf` | `string` | optional | Backend conf value (sccache: "file:///dir", "s3://bucket/…"). |

## `[worktree]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base` | `string` | optional | Worktree parent dir — runs land at `&lt;base&gt;-&lt;repo&gt;-&lt;sha12&gt;`. A leading `~/` expands to `$HOME` at load. |

## `[worker]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` | `list` | optional | Labels this box carries (e.g. \["arch=arm64"]). A job whose `runs_on` requirements are all satisfied here is claimable; unlabeled jobs are claimable by anyone. |
| `node` | `string` | optional | Hypha/peregrin node base URL for the entity-plane worker (`tamias-driver-bupha worker`, P-002) — e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:18787`. Absent = the entity worker has no node to poll (the retired redis pull-queue path is gone — T-049). |
| `node_token_env` | `string` | optional | Env-var NAME holding the node's bearer credential — resolved through the secret chain (env → cuora → `~/.config/bupha/env`), the same rule as `token_env`/ `secret_env`: the config stores the NAME, never the value. `peregrin pair`/`hypha pair` mints the token; store it under this name (e.g. `PEREGRIN_TOKEN`). Absent = unauthenticated calls (dev nodes). |
| `events_url` | `string` | optional | Full URL the worker POSTs `ci.job.completed` to — the `/api/events/inject` route of the campaign host (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:29173/api/events/inject` for `campaign serve`). Absent = `{node}/api/events/inject` — the entity node's own ingest, which fans out to `kind="campaign"` entities, NOT to `campaign serve` supervised campaigns. Set this when campaigns run under `campaign serve` so the completion signal reaches their trigger injectors. |
| `fork_token_env` | `string` | optional | Env-var NAME holding a git credential (PAT/token) used to authenticate `git fetch &lt;cloneUrl&gt;` for fork-PR ci-jobs (T-073 remainder — a fork of a private repo is itself private). Resolved through the secret chain (env → cuora → `~/.config/bupha/env`), the same NAME-only rule as `node_token_env`: the value never lands in this config, in argv, or in the worker's env — the worker materializes a git credential-helper script (under the config dir) that re-resolves the NAME at fetch time, so only the fork fetch sees the credential. A fine-grained PAT that reads both the base org and the fork works here; fork creds that differ from origin creds get their own NAME. Absent = fork fetches ride whatever credential machinery the box already has (global credential helpers, `url.insteadOf`, `gh auth setup-git`) — public forks need nothing. |

## `[[repo.jobs]]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | required | Job name — path-safe `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`, non-empty. Lands in worktree paths (`&lt;base&gt;-&lt;repo&gt;-&lt;job&gt;-&lt;sha12&gt;`), fleet claim keys and the default status context (`&lt;context&gt;/&lt;job&gt;`). |
| `branch` | `string` | optional | The ref this job watches (default: the repo's `branch`). |
| `runner` | `RunnerCfg` | optional | Per-job runner override — replaces the repo/global runner for this job only. |
| `queue` | `"latest" | "all"` | optional | Queue policy for this job — `latest` (default) or `all`. Falls back to the repo's `queue`. |
| `context` | `string` | optional | Status context override (default: `"&lt;status.context&gt;/&lt;job name&gt;"`). |
| `runs_on` | `list` | optional | Label requirements — overrides the repo's `runs_on` for this job only (job -> repo -> \[] inheritance, like runner/queue). |
| `retry` | `u32` | optional | Retry count override — job -> repo -> 0 inheritance. |

## `[runner]` — kind `dagger`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `function` | `string` | optional | — |
| `shards` | `string` | optional | — |
| `jobs` | `string` | optional | — |
| `dogfood_jobs` | `string` | optional | — |
| `sequential` | `bool` | optional | — |
| `sccache_conf` | `string` | optional | sccache conf passed as `--sccache-conf` (resolved from `[cache]` by the composition root). |
| `cli_source` | `string` | optional | — |
| `extra_args` | `list` | optional | — |

## `[runner]` — kind `shell`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cmd` | `string` | optional | — |
| `isolate` | `string` | optional | "scope" → the job runs in its own systemd user scope so a fat job gets OOM-killed alone instead of taking the watcher down with it. Anything else → plain child process. |
| `memory_max` | `string` | optional | `MemoryMax` for the scope ("9G", "4096M") — required for the isolation to bound anything; without it the scope only groups processes. |

## `[runner]` — kind `ssh`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `remote` | `string` | optional | Remote host ("user@host"; ssh config resolves auth). |
| `remote_dir` | `string` | optional | Remote parent dir — each run syncs into its own `&lt;remote_dir&gt;/&lt;key&gt;-&lt;sha12&gt;` subdir. |
| `cmd` | `string` | optional | Command run remotely (fed to `bash -s`). |

## `[runner]` — kind `container`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `string` | required | Image the pipeline runs in (required). |
| `cmd` | `string` | optional | Shell command executed inside the container. |
| `engine` | `string` | optional | Engine binary — `"podman"` (default) or `"docker"`. |
| `network` | `string` | optional | Network mode — `"none"` default (isolated); `"host"`/`"bridge"` for pipelines that genuinely need outbound. |

## `[runner]` — kind `gha`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflow` | `WorkflowSel` | optional | Pin workflow file(s) instead of discovering every `on.push`-matching file under `.github/workflows/`. Entries resolve against `.github/workflows/` first, then the worktree root. |

## Constraints

* `queue = "all"` rejects `cancel_running = true` at load —
  killing a run would silently drop a promised commit.
* `runner.kind` and `trigger.kind`/`status.kind` resolve to impl
  crates; unknown kinds fail at `bupha doctor`/startup.
* `deny_unknown_fields`: typos in field names fail the load.

# Architecture

> **Binary surface (ADR-0006 amendment).** bupha's shipped surface
> is the engine library plus `tamias-driver-bupha` — tamias
> bundles (`type: bupha`) deploy provider units that exec the
> driver's `host` verb, which runs the watcher engine
> (`bupha-watch`) in-process. The `bupha` CLI binary is a
> dev/debug harness (`run`/`doctor`/`import`/`watch`); production
> webhook ingress is a peregrin campaign (ADR-0007), with the
> bupha webhook listener as the standalone/dev fallback.

bupha is a port/adapter monorepo: every external concern sits
behind a trait (a *port*), and each integration is a crate that
implements it (an *impl*). `bupha-core` is the pure domain — config
shape, queue semantics, shared primitives — and depends on nothing
outside itself; `bupha-cli` is the engine lib + clap tree
(`command()`/`run_from`) the dev harness and the driver's `cli`/
`ops` surfaces share (the deployed composition is
`tamias-driver-bupha` + tamias provider units).

## Crate map

| crate | layer | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `bupha-core` | domain | bupha domain core: config types, job queues, shared primitives — no ports, no integrations |
| `bupha-access` | port | Access port: who may trigger a repo |
| `bupha-attest` | port | Attest port: signed run provenance (SLSA-style predicate) |
| `bupha-cache` | port | Cache port: artifact-cache backend for runners |
| `bupha-queue` | port | QueueStore port: queue persistence |
| `bupha-runner` | port | Runner port: how a job becomes a spawned process |
| `bupha-status` | port | StatusSink port: where run outcomes are reported |
| `bupha-telemetry` | port | Telemetry port: fire-and-forget pipeline events |
| `bupha-trigger` | port | Source port: where pushes come from — forge webhooks, WAL polls, … |
| `bupha-access-file` | adapter | Access adapter: allowlist of forge logins from config |
| `bupha-access-forge` | adapter | Access adapter: forge collaborator-permission check |
| `bupha-attest-file` | adapter | Attest adapter: SLSA-shape predicate JSON per run (unsigned v1) |
| `bupha-attest-sigstore` | adapter | Attest adapter: cosign-signed run predicates (needs cosign + key) |
| `bupha-audit-file` | adapter | Audit adapter: append access/outcome decisions to a JSONL file |
| `bupha-cache-sccache` | adapter | Cache impl: sccache-compatible conf (file/S3/R2/GCS via conf) |
| `bupha-config-file` | adapter | File impl of the config port — scarab-config discovery (explicit → $BUPHA_CONFIG → ./bupha.\* → ~/.config/bupha/) + local TOML/YAML format dispatch for bupha_core::Config |
| `bupha-container` | adapter | Runner adapter: unprivileged container (podman/docker), network-off |
| `bupha-dagger` | adapter | Runner impl: `dagger call &lt;fn&gt;` per job |
| `bupha-driver` | adapter | tamias-driver-bupha — pavo view driver over bupha's on-disk run/queue state (read-only) |
| `bupha-gha` | adapter | Runner impl: .github/workflows/*.yml executed natively — GitHub Actions as CI dialect |
| `bupha-gha-runner` | adapter | GitHub Actions self-hosted runner — speaks the actions/runner broker protocol so repos can runs-on: \[self-hosted, bupha] |
| `bupha-github` | adapter | GitHub impl: push-webhook trigger + commit-status sink |
| `bupha-history` | adapter | Run-history adapter: JSONL records per finished run |
| `bupha-http` | adapter | Runner impl: remote execution via HTTP agent (tar worktree + poll) |
| `bupha-plane` | adapter | ci-job entity plane — hypha EntityPlane impl for the bupha↔hypha/peregrin seam (P-002) |
| `bupha-secret-cuora` | adapter | Secret impl: cuora broker via the cuora CLI (canonical secrets story, T-056) |
| `bupha-shell` | adapter | Runner impl: bash -c \<cmd> per job — no containers |
| `bupha-ssh` | adapter | Runner impl: remote execution over ssh (rsync worktree + run) |
| `bupha-sturn` | adapter | sturn source impl: reads refs/sturn/* WAL state out of a clone via git plumbing |
| `bupha-telemetry-otel` | adapter | Telemetry adapter: OpenMetrics textfile for Prometheus |
| `bupha-watch` | adapter | bupha watcher engine host — trigger → queue → runner → status pipeline shared by `bupha watch` and `tamias-driver-bupha host` |
| `bupha` | binary | bupha — queue engine for event-driven jobs: shipped as CI |

`modules/dagger/` (Python SDK) is the shared pipeline module
the dev CLI's `bupha init` installs into consumer repos — pinned
to a sha.

## Sources — the ingest edge

bupha is a queue engine: `source → queue → effect`. Everything
in front of the queue is a `Source` — a long-running ingest that
emits normalized `(repo, ref, sha, sender)` pushes; everything
behind it (queues, runner, status sinks) is source-agnostic. A
watcher process — `tamias-driver-bupha host` in deployed units,
`bupha watch` in the dev harness — runs every configured source
and feeds one shared ingest path.

| source            | config                                   | emits on                        |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `github-webhook`  | `trigger.kind = "github"` (+ `[trigger]` listener, secrets, tunnel) | verified `push`/`pull_request` deliveries (`[[repo]] events`) |
| `sturn-wal`       | `[trigger.sturn]` + `[[repo]] sturn = true` | `Op::Snapshot` WAL events       |

`pull_request` deliveries are opt-in per repo (`events`): the PR
head sha runs in a worktree while `branch`/job filters evaluate
the *base* ref — a `refs/heads/main` gate covers PRs targeting
main with no extra config.

`Trigger` is the narrower per-request port a webhook `Source`
drives — is this our event, which repo (untrusted hint), does the
signature verify, what does the payload ask for. New forges mean a
new `Trigger` impl reusing the same webhook listener; new *kinds*
of ingest (gitlab webhook, cron, poll-ref, file-watch) are new
`Source` impls — neither touches the queue.

## Webhook request flow

The `github-webhook` source's per-request pipeline (byte-stable —
routing and statuses are part of the contract):

```
POST /hook
  → 1. path check (404 otherwise)
  → 2. read body (≤ 2 MiB)
  → 3. repo hint — untrusted peek at repository.full_name,
       selects the watched [[repo]] and its secret; an
       unwatched repo 404s (it can never verify)
  → 4. signature verify (Trigger port — github impl: HMAC
       sha256, constant-time; key = repo's secret_env,
       falling back to trigger.secret_env)
  → 5. dedup delivery id (bounded 10k ring; github impl uses
       X-GitHub-Delivery)
  → 6. parse — skip deletes/zero-sha; revision must be path-safe
  → 7. route — git_ref selects every job of the repo watching it
       ([[repo.jobs]] entries, or the repo's implicit pipeline);
       forge-attested sender checked against the access policy
  → 8. enqueue — one queue per job; a push fan-outs into every
       matched queue; jobs this box's `[worker] labels` can't
       satisfy belong to the ci-job entity plane instead; persist
       via QueueStore (dev `json` file)
  → 9. one global worker — Vcs fetch, detached worktree
       at <base>-<repo>[-<job>]-<sha12>
  → 10. spawn run handle (token via env:// name, never argv)
  → 11. status — pending → success/error; superseded and
        cancelled shas get honest error statuses. Runners may
        report sub-job verdicts (`Runner::status_reports`) —
        the gha dialect emits one per expanded workflow job /
        matrix leg, posted under `<context>/<workflow>/<job>`
        via `StatusSink::post_ctx` before the aggregate lands
```

## Queue semantics

Queues are per *job*: a `[[repo]]` is one implicit pipeline unless
it declares `[[repo.jobs]]`, in which case each job gets an
independent queue (`name:job` keys), branch filter, runner and
status context. One push fan-outs into every job queue whose
`branch` matches the ref — same-repo jobs are independent of each
other (latest-wins on one never touches another's pending slot, and
`cancel_running` only kills its own job's in-flight run).

| policy             | pending           | on new push                                                                                           | use for  |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `latest` (default) | 1 sha             | supersedes pending; `cancel_running` may kill in-flight                                               | CI gates |
| `all`              | bounded FIFO (32) | appends; oldest evicted past cap; `cancel_running` rejected at load — it would drop a promised commit | releases |

Persistence: accepted work writes through the `QueueStore` port
(the dev `json` file under `worktree.base`; the durable path is
the ci-job entity plane — see [distributed
runners](../how-to/distributed-runners.md)) and on restart the
interrupted `running` sha is re-queued at the front.

One **global worker** serializes runs across all repos — a second
push queues behind the in-flight job. Deliberate (one box, bounded
resource use), not a hang: `journalctl --user -u bupha-watch` shows
the queue moving.

## Security model

* mandatory HMAC (constant-time compare) — unauthenticated payloads
  never reach the queue
* per-repo webhook secrets (`[[repo]] secret_env`, falling back to
  `trigger.secret_env`) — the repo is resolved before verify, so a
  hook admin on one repo can't forge signed pushes for another
* body cap, delivery-id replay dedup, hex-sha validation before the
  value touches paths or status URLs
* webhook takeover is exact-URL only; hook API calls are timed out
* config names secrets (`secret_env`/`token_env`) — values resolve
  env → cuora (`cuora://bupha/<NAME>`, canonical, T-056; fleet
  secrets migrated, T-059) → `~/.config/bupha/env`
  (0600 — dev-mode / no-cuora fallback; keyring leg dropped
  post-T-077); the runner gets
  the token through its own mechanism (`env://` for dagger)

## Extending

| to add…                     | write…                                 | core changes? |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| push source (cron, poll)    | `Source` adapter crate                  | no            |
| forge (gitea/gitlab)        | `Trigger` + `StatusSink` adapter crate  | no            |
| pipeline backend            | `Runner` adapter crate                  | no            |
| ingress (fly/tailscale)     | `Tunnel` adapter crate                  | no            |

---
# The release model

bupha releases itself — there is no hosted CI and no release tool
in the loop. (The release verbs live on the dev CLI — `bupha
deploy release`, `scripts/release.sh` — maintainer tooling, not
user surface; ADR-0006.) The org release plane is **tarsi**
(`tarsi-serve` ops — project ADR-0005): `scripts/release.sh` is
being converted to a thin shim over it (PL-014 E1), and until then
this script implements the same tag-only + `tamias publish` model
directly. Two deliberate phases:

## Phase 1 — the explicit seed

The dev CLI's `bupha deploy release` runs once, by hand: it reads
cargo metadata, verifies the workspace shares one version, tags
`{repo}-v{version}`, and pushes the tag. (`--dry-run` prints the
tag without touching anything.)

Why explicit? A tag is the boundary of "this sha is a release" —
everything after it is derived. There is no crates.io publish
anymore: org policy keeps every repo but tamias off crates.io, and
the bupha crates are internal lib-only engines anyway.

## Phase 2 — push-driven forever after

From then on a release is *just another bupha job*: a push to `main`
hits the webhook, queues latest-wins, and runs `scripts/release.sh`
in a detached worktree under the shell runner.

The script:

1. diffs release-worthy paths (crates, `libraries/`, `modules/`,
   workspace manifests, the script itself) since the last
   `bupha-v*` tag
2. `cargo set-version --workspace --bump patch` — every member
   inherits `version.workspace`, so one bump moves them all, along
   with the `workspace.dependencies` reqs and `Cargo.lock`
3. syncs the version refs in `libraries/bupha/tamias.yaml` and the
   README's install example
4. commits `release: bump bupha to <ver>`, tags `bupha-v<ver>`,
   pushes

User-facing distribution is the tamias pack — after the tag the
operator runs `tamias publish libraries/bupha` to ship
`9aia:bupha@<ver>` to the org registry (the pack's bundled
`tamias-driver-bupha` binary is the whole install artifact).

The 5-minute sleep at the top isn't a hack — it's the debounce
window. Combined with `queue = "latest"` + `cancel_running`, rapid
push bursts collapse to one release of the newest sha; killed runs
get an honest "cancelled" status.

## Why this shape

* **No release-plz / GHA**: the point of the project is that CI is a
  local loop — depending on hosted CI to ship it would be
  self-defeating. `release.sh` is deliberately boring bash so it can
  run as a plain `cmd` under `runner.kind = "shell"`.
* **Latest-wins, not `all`**: a release that misses an intermediate
  push loses nothing — the tag lands on HEAD, which contains
  everything. `queue = "all"` is for pipelines where each sha's run
  is individually meaningful.
* **Tag-only, publish-by-hand**: the irreversible step moved off
  crates.io entirely — the org registry publish is an explicit
  operator act (`tamias publish`), not part of the release script.

Host prerequisites: `cargo-edit` and `git`. Multi-arch binaries
arrive when the remote-runner pair lands — see TODO.
