# Crate scope audit — bupha under ADR-0006

Per-crate ruling for every crate in `crates/`, against ADR-0006
("bupha is CI semantics only — substrate is hypha/peregrin,
distribution is tamias") and the P-002 ci-job ops contract.

Rulings:

* **KEEP** — CI semantics or runner/dialect/forge/status knowledge
  that stays in bupha.
* **MIGRATE** — stateful/infra machinery that becomes a hypha-side
  impl or dies in favor of ci-job entities. Target home noted.
* **DIE** — fully subsumed, no port value.
* **SPLIT** — crate mixes semantics + machinery; noted per half.
* **DEV** — survives only as the in-process dev/test harness
  (ADR-0006: "ports stay, impls get swapped").

## The table

| Crate | Ruling | Reason | Target home |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bupha-core` | KEEP | Canonical job spec, `Queue`/`QueuePolicy`/`MAX_PENDING`, `is_valid_sha`/`is_valid_key`, `WatchedRepo`, config types — the pure semantics P-002 pins as the plane's spec. Gains `cijob` transition functions. | stays |
| `bupha-access` | KEEP | "Who may trigger" — sender authorization is ingest semantics; `sender` is forge-attested. | stays |
| `bupha-access-file` | KEEP | Allowlist policy impl — CI-ingress policy, not generic infra. | stays |
| `bupha-access-forge` | KEEP | Forge collaborator-permission check — forge knowledge is bupha's. | stays |
| `bupha-attest` | KEEP | Run-provenance port (SLSA-style predicate) — attestation is a CI deliverable. | stays |
| `bupha-attest-file` | KEEP | Predicate-file impl of `Attest`. | stays |
| `bupha-attest-sigstore` | KEEP | cosign-signed predicate impl. | stays |
| `bupha-audit-file` | KEEP | JSONL audit of access/run decisions — CI observability. Optional feature; the ci-job entity index may subsume it in hosted mode (open question). | stays |
| `bupha-cache` | KEEP | Port only *renders conf text* the runner consumes (sccache is external) — runner-facing semantics, not a stateful cache. The worktree/build cache concern belongs to substrate, but this crate never held state. | stays |
| `bupha-cache-sccache` | KEEP | Conf renderer for sccache-compatible backends. | stays |
| `bupha-cli` | SPLIT/DEV | Per ADR-0006 amendment there is no user-facing `bupha` CLI. `watch`/`worker`/`agent`/`run`/`import`/`doctor` survive as the dev/test harness (single-box `bupha-node` + embedded queue); lifecycle verbs (`deploy`/`service`/`destroy`) are already driver/tamias surface. The binary eventually dissolves into `tamias-driver-bupha worker` + a dev binary. | dev binary + driver |
| `bupha-cloudflared` | MIGRATE | Named/quick tunnel provider — generic ingress plumbing. Webhook ingress is peregrin's (P-002/T-055); tunnel lifecycle is hypha-service territory. | hypha tunnel impl (or dies if peregrin ships one) |
| `bupha-config` | KEEP | Config port over the CI fleet/repo model — domain-shaped, not generic config machinery. | stays |
| `bupha-config-file` | KEEP | Path resolution + syntax dispatch. | stays |
| `bupha-config-toml` | KEEP | TOML parser impl. | stays |
| `bupha-config-yaml` | KEEP | YAML parser impl (`fleet.toml`/`bupha.yaml` are the standard). | stays |
| `bupha-container` | KEEP | Runner impl — unprivileged container exec is CI-runner semantics. | stays |
| `bupha-dagger` | KEEP | Runner impl — `dagger call` per job. | stays |
| `bupha-dotenv` | MIGRATE | `KEY=VAL` secret file — generic secret plumbing, not CI semantics. hypha already ships `hypha-dotenv`; under a cuora story (T-056) it dies outright. | hypha-secret impls / cuora (T-056) |
| `bupha-driver` | KEEP+EXTEND | `tamias-driver-bupha` is the distribution surface *and* the future worker host (P-002 §4 `worker` verb). `data.rs` moves from `queue.redb` reads to the ci-job entity index when hosted mode lands. | stays — gains `worker` verb + ci-jobs view |
| `bupha-gha` | KEEP | The workflow dialect — parse/plan/script/executor for `.github/workflows/*.yml`. Core CI semantics; also feeds T-050 (self-hosted GHA runner — reserved name `gha-runner`, T-054). | stays |
| `bupha-git` | KEEP | `Vcs` impl via git CLI — worktree/sync primitives every runner needs. | stays |
| `bupha-github` | KEEP | Trigger parse/verify (push normalization) + `StatusSink` commit-status posting — both halves are CI semantics (P-002 keeps normalization + worker-side status posting in bupha). | stays |
| `bupha-history` | KEEP (dev/optional) | JSONL run records for `bupha runs`/`log`. In hosted mode the ci-job entity index *is* the history; keep as dev-mode/optional feature, candidate to fold later. | stays (dev) |
| `bupha-http` | KEEP | Runner impl — remote exec via `bupha agent` (tar worktree + poll). Runner semantics; known auth caveats tracked as issues. | stays |
| `bupha-keyring` | MIGRATE | OS-keyring secret impl — generic secret plumbing. hypha ships `hypha-keyring`; cuora is the org broker story (T-056). | hypha-keyring / cuora (T-056) |
| `bupha-queue` | KEEP (dev only) | `QueueStore`/`WorkQueue` port + `MemWorkQueue` — P-002 keeps the port and in-process impl for dev/test; the distributed path is the ci-job entity plane, not this port. | stays (dev/test) |
| `bupha-queue-lease` | DIE | `Fence`/`TryClaim` semantics are absorbed verbatim into the ci-job entity (`fence` counter + `leaseExpiresAt` + `ci.claim` CAS, P-002 §3). No port value once the plane lands; dev mode doesn't need it (`MemWorkQueue` always claims). | → `bupha-plane` entity state |
| `bupha-queue-redb` | MIGRATE | Embedded durable queue — single-node state machinery. The entity plane replaces it even single-box; if hypha wants a local durable queue impl it can adopt the redb code hypha-side. Dev path uses `MemWorkQueue`. | hypha-side queue impl (or DIE — open question) |
| `bupha-queue-redis` | MIGRATE | Networked queue impl (SET NX claim + INCR fence) — textbook substrate. The ci-job entity CAS + outbox is the distributed queue. | hypha-side queue impl |
| `bupha-runner` | KEEP | Runner port — `RunCtx`/`RunHandle`/`Runner` is the seam every runner impl (shell/container/ssh/http/dagger/gha) plugs into. | stays |
| `bupha-secret` | DECIDE (T-056) | Secret-resolution port. If cuora wins the secrets story the port dies (cuora refs replace named-secret lookup); if env-file/keyring survives it stays thin. Tentative: DIE under cuora. | cuora / hypha-secret (T-056) |
| `bupha-service` | DIE | OS service-lifecycle port — generic infra now owned by tamias-provider (`tamias-deploy -systemd`/`-windows`) and hypha-service. Bupha's only consumer was its own (dead) CLI verbs. | tamias / hypha-service |
| `bupha-shell` | KEEP | Runner impl — `bash -c` exec. | stays |
| `bupha-ssh` | KEEP | Runner impl — remote exec over ssh/rsync. Runner semantics. | stays |
| `bupha-status` | KEEP | `StatusSink` port — workers post forge commit statuses on `ci.complete` (they hold forge creds via `token_env`); the plane records outcome but does not post (P-002 §5). | stays |
| `bupha-sturn` | KEEP | Trigger impl — polls `refs/sturn/*` WAL → normalized `Push`es with SSH-verified sender attestation. Event→push normalization is CI semantics; sturn itself is a sibling repo. | stays |
| `bupha-systemd` | MIGRATE | User-unit rendering — generic service lifecycle. `tamias-deploy -systemd` already owns this; the driver's `deploy` verb should consume tamias's surface instead. | tamias-deploy-systemd / hypha-systemd |
| `bupha-telemetry` | KEEP | Telemetry port over CI-shaped run events (`Queued`/`Started`/`Finished`) — observability semantics; optional feature. | stays |
| `bupha-telemetry-otel` | KEEP | OpenMetrics textfile impl. Note overlap with `hypha-telemetry` (OTLP) — different export shape, both may coexist; revisit if hypha-telemetry gains textfile. | stays |
| `bupha-trigger` | KEEP | Source/`Trigger` port + `Push`/`Verdict`/`PushOutcome` — the normalization contract every ingress (webhook, sturn, future gitlab) drives. | stays |
| `bupha-tunnel` | DIE | Port exists solely to expose the webhook listener publicly. Production ingress is peregrin's; dev mode can use a hypha tunnel impl or `direct`. No CI semantics in the trait. | → hypha (if a generic tunnel port is wanted) |
| `bupha-vcs` | KEEP | VCS port — sync/worktree/tag ops the runner pipeline needs. | stays |
| `bupha-webhook` | SPLIT | The `Trigger`-driving + signature/dedup logic's durable value is subsumed: deterministic entity ids (`ci:{key}:{sha}:{attempt}`) dedup replays for free (P-002 §1), so the `Seen` ring dies with the listener. The tiny_http accept-loop harness → dev-mode only; production ingress is a peregrin campaign listener that normalizes via `bupha-trigger` then `POST /api/entities` (T-055). | harness → dev; dedup → entity ids |

## Incoming

* **`bupha-plane`** (new, P-002) — KEEP. Thin `hypha_http::EntityPlane`
  adapter holding ci-job entity state and dispatching `ci.*` ops; the
  pure transition math stays in `bupha-core`. First bupha→hypha dep —
  confirm acceptable (P-002 open question 1).

## Key judgment calls

* **Queue family**: the *semantics* (`Queue`, supersede/retry math,
  `MAX_PENDING`) stay in `bupha-core` as the spec the plane mirrors;
  the *port + in-process impl* (`bupha-queue`) stay for dev/test per
  P-002; the *distributed impls* (`-redb`, `-redis`) and the *lease
  port* migrate/die — fencing becomes entity state (`fence` +
  `leaseExpiresAt` + op CAS), not a separate port.
* **Cache**: `bupha-cache`/`-sccache` are KEEP — they render runner
  conf, they don't *are* a cache. The substrate cache concern
  (worktree/build artifacts across nodes) is hypha's and was never
  these crates' job.
* **Ingress trio** (`webhook`/`trigger`/`sturn`): normalization
  (`Trigger`, `Push`, `Verdict`, sturn WAL→push) is KEEP — it's the
  "forge event → job spec" half of ADR-0006. Listener harnesses are
  dev-mode; production ingress is peregrin's.
* **Secrets trio** (`secret`/`keyring`/`dotenv`): judged generic infra,
  not CI semantics — but the ruling is gated on T-056 (cuora vs env vs
  keyring). hypha already ships `hypha-{secret,keyring,dotenv}` impls,
  so MIGRATE has a ready home; under cuora they all DIE.
* **Service/lifecycle** (`service`/`systemd`/`tunnel`/`cloudflared`):
  all generic host machinery — tamias (deploy/provider) + hypha
  (service/systemd) own it now. DIE or MIGRATE; nothing here is CI
  semantics.
* **Enterprise surfaces** (`access*`/`attest*`/`audit-file`/`history`/
  `telemetry*`): KEEP as optional bupha features — they encode
  CI-specific policy (who may trigger, run provenance, audit trail),
  not generic substrate. Only `history` is a maybe-fold into the
  entity index later.
* **`bupha-cli`**: SPLIT — dev harness survives, user-facing binary
  dies per the ADR-0006 amendment; `tamias-driver-bupha worker` is the
  production worker host.

## Open questions

1. **Secrets story (T-056)** gates `bupha-secret`/`-keyring`/`-dotenv`:
   cuora → all three die; env/keyring → port stays thin, impls
   duplicate hypha's. Pick before migrating.
2. **`bupha-queue-redb`**: migrate the redb code hypha-side as a local
   durable queue impl, or let the entity plane cover single-box too
   (dev uses `MemWorkQueue`) and DIE it? Lean: DIE unless hypha wants
   a non-entity queue.
3. **`bupha-plane` home** (P-002 Q1): bupha crate dep'ing on
   `hypha-http` vs plane code inside `peregrin-node`. Audit assumes
   the bupha crate.
4. **`history`/`audit-file` vs entity index**: do ci-job entities +
   `ci.status` fully replace `history.jsonl`/`audit.log` in hosted
   mode, making both dev-only? Probably yes; confirm before deleting
   read paths the driver still uses.
5. **`bupha-telemetry-otel` vs `hypha-telemetry`**: keep the
   OpenMetrics textfile impl in bupha, or does hypha-telemetry absorb
   textfile export? Different export shapes today — keep for now.
6. **Tunnel**: does hypha/peregrin want a generic tunnel port at all,
   or is ingress exposure always a campaign/deploy concern (named
   tunnel via tamias)? Determines whether `bupha-tunnel`'s trait
   migrates or just dies.

## Resolution — T-077 (landed)

With T-055 (ADR-0007: ingress is peregrin-owned, bupha webhook
surfaces are standalone/dev mode) and T-056 (cuora canonical,
T-059 migration verified) done, the remaining MIGRATE/DIE crates
were retired in three commits on `main`:

| Crate | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `bupha-secret` | **DIE** — trait identical to `hypha_secret::Secrets`; consumers take the hypha git dep directly. |
| `bupha-keyring` | **DIE → `hypha-keyring`** with `service = "bupha"` so pre-cuora keyring entries still resolve. |
| `bupha-dotenv` | **DIE → `hypha-dotenv`** — `~/.config/bupha/env` path/format unchanged. |
| `bupha-secret-cuora` | **KEEP** — the canonical store; now implements `hypha_secret::Secrets` (already wrapped `hypha-secret-cuora`). |
| `bupha-service` | **DIE** — one impl (`bupha-systemd`), consumers used free fns/struct, not the trait. |
| `bupha-systemd` | **DIE → `hypha-systemd`** — unit render/control via `write_unit`/`enable`/`disable`/`status`/`restart`/`unit_path`/`default_unit_dir`. Bupha-shaped helpers (`write_env_skeleton`, `service_logs`, strict daemon-reload on destroy, `SystemdService` wrapper) folded into `bupha-cli`'s `deploy` module. Unit diffs: bare name + `.service` suffix, quoted ExecStart argv, `EnvironmentFile=-`, `Restart=on-failure`. |
| `bupha-tunnel` + `bupha-cloudflared` | **FOLDED → `bupha-watch::tunnel`** — ADR-0007 keeps them as the standalone/dev-mode ingress; no hypha tunnel impl exists or is wanted (ingress exposure is a deploy/campaign concern). |
| `bupha-webhook` | **FOLDED → `bupha-watch::webhook`** — same reasoning; `tiny_http` dep moved to bupha-watch. |

Open questions 1 and 6 are thereby resolved: cuora won the secrets
story (legacy keyring/dotenv legs survive only as hypha-backed
fallbacks in the dev chain), and no generic tunnel port migrates —
the trait lives on inside `bupha-watch` for standalone mode only.

url: /bupha/explanation/gha-dogfood.md

# Dogfood: real GitHub Actions workflows through `runner.kind = "gha"`

Parity report for the `gha` dialect (org-ledger T-003). Method:
real `.github/workflows/ci.yml` files from public Rust repos —
the 9aia org repos themselves carry **no** GitHub workflows (CI
is hooks + myco/sturn, not GHA), so "real" means upstream public
repos — dropped into a scratch git repo and run through
`bupha run` with `runner.kind = "gha"`. Unsupported constructs
were then peeled iteratively (each `spawn failed:` error fixed,
re-run) until each workflow planned **and executed**, recording
every error along the way.

Workflows tested (fetched 2026-11, upstream `main`/`master`):

| repo | file | jobs | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dtolnay/anyhow | `ci.yml` (146 lines) | 9 | hard error at spawn; plans+executes after peeling ~35 unsupported constructs |
| serde-rs/serde | `ci.yml` (179 lines) | 10 | hard error at spawn; plans+executes after peeling ~40 unsupported constructs |
| BurntSushi/ripgrep | `ci.yml` (291 lines) | 6 | hard error at spawn; plans+executes after peeling ~20 unsupported constructs |
| synthetic subset port | — | 3 | **full pass** — every supported feature exercised green |

## First-error results (unmodified workflows)

| workflow | first `spawn failed:` error |
| --- | --- |
| anyhow `ci.yml` | `gha: ci.yml.jobs.pre_ci: unsupported key 'uses'` — job-level reusable-workflow call (`uses: dtolnay/.github/.github/workflows/pre_ci.yml@master`, line 17) |
| serde `ci.yml` | `gha: ci.yml.jobs.test: unsupported key 'timeout-minutes'` (line 19) |
| ripgrep `ci.yml` | `gha: ci.yml.jobs.test.env.TARGET_FLAGS: expected a scalar, got null` — **bug, fixed** (see below); next error is `jobs.test.strategy: unsupported key 'fail-fast'` (line 51) |

Parse is all-or-nothing per file and stops at the first error —
the tables below are the *complete* inventory obtained by peeling.

## Unsupported-syntax inventory hit during peeling

Every real workflow hit the same wall, in roughly this order:

| construct | where it appears | gha verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| job-level `uses:` (reusable workflows) | anyhow `pre_ci` (L17) | hard error `unsupported key 'uses'` |
| job `if:` | anyhow L22,54,73,85,98,114,126,140; serde L143,157,173; ripgrep step-level mostly | hard error `unsupported key 'if'` |
| `timeout-minutes` | every job in anyhow/serde | hard error `unsupported key 'timeout-minutes'` |
| `strategy.fail-fast` | anyhow L25,57; serde L44,61,85; ripgrep L51 | hard error `unsupported key 'fail-fast'` |
| step `if:` | anyhow L37,40,45; serde L75,79; ripgrep L123,131,143,159,185,193,201,240,258,273,281,293 | hard error `unsupported key 'if'` |
| step `continue-on-error` | anyhow L49; serde L29 | hard error `unsupported key 'continue-on-error'` |
| `uses:` ≠ `actions/checkout` | `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` (everywhere), `dtolnay/install`, `actions/upload-artifact`, `docker/setup-docker-action`, `actions/cache`, `actions/setup-node`, `docker://pandoc/…` | hard error `unsupported 'uses: …'` — *`dtolnay/rust-toolchain` and the artifact actions have since landed; `actions/setup-*`/`actions/cache`/`docker://`/local paths still error* |
| `strategy.matrix.include` | ripgrep L53–117, mdBook main.yml | `expected a scalar, got mapping` |
| complex ${{ }} expressions | serde L58 job name (`matrix.os == 'windows' && … \|\| ''`), ripgrep `startsWith(...)`, `hashFiles(...)`, `steps.*.outputs.*` | hard error `unsupported expression` — *`steps.*.outputs.*`/`needs.*.outputs.*` since wired (T-069); the rest still error* |
| `env:` null values | ripgrep L40–42 (`TARGET_FLAGS:` empty) | **was a bug — fixed** (null now coerces to `""`) |
| step `with:` on any `uses:` | ripgrep L133–135, L249–257 | **was a bug — fixed** (`with` was missing from the step key allowlist; `actions/checkout` `with:` inputs now accepted, `with.path` still errors, `with` on `run:` errors) |
| job `name:` ${{ }} | serde L41,58,82; anyhow L20,53 | **was a bug — fixed** (names are now interpolated; unsupported expressions in names now error loudly instead of passing through verbatim) |

Triggers `pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`,
`merge_group` are silently ignored — only `on.push` selects. A
workflow with *no* `push` trigger parses fine and simply never
matches (`no on.push workflow matched` → vacuous success).

## Execution parity (peeled workflows)

Once peeled, all three workflows **plan and execute**: jobs run
sequentially in `needs` topo-order, matrix combos fan out
in parallel (private per-leg worktrees), `actions/checkout` verifies HEAD, step
`env`/`working-directory`/`shell` are honored, and failing `run`
steps fail their job while independent jobs continue — matching
GHA's aggregate-status shape. In the scratch repos the cargo/npm
steps fail fast (no real project/toolchain), so the aggregate
exit is 1 — the *machinery* is what was verified.

A purpose-built subset workflow (matrix 2×2, `needs` chain,
workflow/job/step `env` with ${{ env.\* }}/${{ matrix.\* }}/
${{ github.\* }}, `defaults.run.working-directory` + `shell`,
step `working-directory` override, `shell: sh`,
`actions/checkout` with `with:`, `branches` + `paths-ignore`
filters) passes **fully green**, including correct skip of a
`needs`-dependent job when a matrix leg fails.

## Semantic gaps vs GitHub Actions

> **Update (T-048).** Several gaps below closed since this report:
> `if:` (job+step) now parses a real expression subset — literals,
> `==`/`!=`/`&&`/`||`/`!`/parens, `contains`/`startsWith`/`endsWith`,
> `success()`/`failure()`/`cancelled()`/`always()`, plus
> `needs.*.result`/`steps.*.conclusion` — with the implicit
> `success() &&` wrap; `timeout-minutes` is enforced (GNU `timeout`
> per step, process-group watchdog per job); `strategy.fail-fast`
> cancels remaining matrix legs and `max-parallel` throttles
> parallel legs (each leg gets a private `git worktree`; `1`
> pins the sequential path); `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` lowers to rustup calls;
> `paths` filters now infer the push's `before` sha from
> remote-tracking refs/reflogs/merge-base instead of diffing only
> `HEAD^..HEAD`. Each expanded job that reaches a verdict (every
> workflow job, every matrix leg) now also posts its own commit
> status under `<context>/<workflow>/<job id>[/<matrix>]` — the
> aggregate `ci/bupha[/<job>]` context is unchanged. Parallel
> matrix landed: legs fan out as process groups in per-leg
> worktrees, `fail-fast` kills siblings, and `needs.*.outputs.*`
> resolves to the highest-index successful leg — details in the
> crate README boundaries.
> `actions/upload-artifact`/`actions/download-artifact` also landed
> since (per-run tar store under the run's tmp dir — same-run
> only; see the crate README boundaries), as did `actions/setup-*`
> toolchains, `actions/cache*`, and **composite actions**
> (`uses: ./path` + `owner/repo[/path]@ref` → `runs.using:
> composite` `action.yml`, strict inputs/outputs contract, nested
> to depth 8). `env:` on `uses:` steps now reaches the action.
> `uses: docker://<image>` steps and composite `timeout-minutes`
> have since landed too (`docker run` on the host — docker CLI
> required; the composite timeout is a deadline spanning the
> inlined steps). **Reusable workflows** (`jobs.<id>.uses:` →
> `./.github/workflows/*.yml` or `owner/repo[/path]@<ref>`, with
> `on.workflow_call` inputs/secrets/outputs, graph merge and
> `secrets: inherit`/explicit maps) have since landed as well —
> details in the crate README. The bullets below are
> annotated where they changed.

* **`$GITHUB_ENV` / `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` / `$GITHUB_PATH` /
  `$RUNNER_TEMP` are unset.** `run: echo X=1 >> $GITHUB_ENV` fails
  with `ambiguous redirect`. This is the biggest functional gap —
  ripgrep's cross-install step and anyhow's nightly RUSTFLAGS
  steps depend on it. Filed as **T-060** (linked to T-048).
  *(Superseded: these are now wired — see the crate README; the
  dogfood run predates T-060's landing.)*
* **`runs-on` is advisory.** `windows-latest`/`macos-latest` jobs
  execute locally on the watcher's Linux box — serde's `windows`
  job would "pass" having never run Windows. No platform guard or
  warning today.
* **Matrix legs run in private worktrees** (documented): GHA
  gives each leg a fresh runner checkout; bupha gives each leg a
  `git worktree` under the run's tmp dir, so workspace writes
  stay per-leg (use job `outputs:`/artifacts/`$BUPHA_WORKDIR` to
  share). ripgrep's 17-combo `include` matrix isn't even
  expressible (`include`/`exclude` unsupported) — cartesian
  list-form only.
* **`if:` supported subset only.** The common constructs now work
  (see update note), but the full expression language —
  `hashFiles`, `fromJSON`, `format`, ternary, `runner.*`,
  `strategy.*`, `steps.*.outcome` — still hard-errors loudly.
* **Third-party actions are still mostly the hard wall.**
  `actions/setup-*`, `actions/cache`, `docker://…`,
  local/composite `uses:` paths and reusable-workflow `uses:` all
  error; `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` lowers to rustup calls and
  `actions/upload-artifact`/`actions/download-artifact` share a
  per-run tar store (same-run only — nothing persists across
  runs). Toolchain setup beyond rustup still needs manual
  porting. *(Superseded: `actions/setup-{node,python,go,java,
  dotnet}`, `actions/cache*`, composite `uses:` and `docker://`
  steps have since landed; JS/docker action *definitions*, other
  setup families and reusable-workflow `uses:` still error.)*
  *(Superseded again: reusable-workflow `uses:` has since landed —
  local `./.github/workflows/*.yml` and remote
  `owner/repo[/path]@<ref>` targets, `on.workflow_call` contracts,
  `secrets: inherit`/explicit maps; see the crate README.)*
* **Expression language grew but stays a subset.** `==`, `!=`,
  `&&`, `||`, `!`, parens, `contains`/`startsWith`/`endsWith`,
  status functions and the `needs.*.result`/`steps.*.conclusion`
  refs now work in `if:` and ${{ }} (T-048); no ternary,
  `hashFiles`, `format`, `fromJSON`, or object/array contexts.
* **Reusable workflows landed with honest edges** (T-048) —
  `jobs.<id>.uses:` now resolves local `./.github/workflows/*.yml`
  and remote `owner/repo[/path]@<ref>` callees, binds
  `with:`→`inputs.*` and `secrets:`→`secrets.*`, merges the callee
  graph under `<call>.<job>` ids, and exposes
  `on.workflow_call.outputs` as `needs.<call>.outputs.*`. Still
  unsupported: execution keys on the calling job, callees without
  `on.workflow_call:`, `secrets.*`/`jobs.*` outside the contract,
  nesting past depth 8, and `secrets:` values that aren't scalars
  or ${{ secrets.X }} forwards.
* **`paths` filters infer `before`** (T-048): remote-tracking
  ref → reflog → local branch → merge-base, falling back to the
  tip commit. Multi-commit pushes are covered when the repo still
  has a ref pointing at the push's base; a `before` the clone
  never saw still undercounts (documented boundary).
* **`actions/checkout` ignores `with.ref`/`fetch-depth`** — it is
  a verification no-op; the worktree is already at the pushed sha.
  `with.path` errors.
* **Parse-before-filter**: every candidate workflow file is parsed
  even when its `on.push` filters wouldn't match — a broken
  non-matching workflow still fails the spawn (loud by design,
  differs from GHA which wouldn't evaluate it at all).
* **Timeouts landed; services/containers/concurrency didn't** —
  `timeout-minutes` is enforced at job (watchdog) and step
  (`timeout`) level (T-048); `services:`, `container:`,
  `concurrency:`, `continue-on-error:` remain hard errors.
  Job/step `outputs:` and the `steps.*`/`needs.*` refs are
  supported since T-069.

## Bugs found & fixed in this dogfood

1. **`env:` null values rejected** — `KEY:` (YAML null) errored
   `expected a scalar, got null`; GHA coerces to `""`. Fixed in
   `env_map` + regression test.
2. **Step `with:` unreachable** — `with` was missing from the
   step key allowlist *and* the unsupported list, so
   `actions/checkout` `with:` inputs errored as `unknown key
   'with'` before `parse_uses` could validate them (the `with.path`
   check was dead code). `with` is now allowed on `uses` steps,
   rejected on `run` steps.
3. **Job `name:` never interpolated** — ${{ matrix.\* }} in
   `jobs.<id>.name` passed through verbatim into logs. Names are
   now interpolated like every other field; unsupported
   expressions in names now fail loudly (consistent with the
   subset contract).

## Reproduce

```bash
# scratch repo: git init, commit, drop a real ci.yml into
# .github/workflows/, then:
bupha --config bupha.yaml run   # runner.kind = "gha"
```

`spawn failed: gha: <file>:<path>: <reason>` names the exact YAML
key — peel iteratively to enumerate the full unsupported surface.

---

---
url: /bupha/comparison.md
---
# bupha vs hosted CI

bupha runs push-triggered CI on self-controlled hardware —
not a GHA replacement at fleet scale.

## vs GitHub Actions

|              | bupha                                           | GitHub Actions                    |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| compute      | your box                                        | managed fleet                     |
| queue        | latest-wins + bounded `all`, no cold start      | unlimited parallelism, queue wait |
| secrets      | never leave the machine                         | hosted on GitHub                  |
| cache        | your backend — local disk or your S3/R2/minio   | hosted cache                      |
| pipeline def | your runner — `ci.sh`, dagger module, or a supported subset of `.github/workflows` YAML (`runner.kind = "gha"`) | YAML DSL + marketplace actions    |
| local == CI  | dev CLI `bupha run` is literally the same path   | `act` approximates                |
| batching     | supersede built-in, honest "cancelled" statuses | `concurrency` groups              |
| scale        | one worker, serialized runs                     | matrix/fleet                      |
| cost         | your box only                                   | minutes billing                   |

**When GHA is better:** you need parallelism, matrices across OSes,
hosted macOS/Windows builds, or marketplace actions. **When bupha
fits:** instant feedback on self-owned hardware, secrets that
never leave the machine, warm caches on self-owned storage, no
runner fleet to operate (the `gha` dialect runs a documented
workflow subset — not full Actions parity).

## vs others

* **Jenkins/Buildkite** — bupha is a single binary with a TOML file,
  not a server product to operate.
* **Woodpecker/Forgejo CI** — bupha is forge-webhook driven and much
  smaller; those are full pipeline platforms.
* **self-hosted GHA runner** — bupha is lighter (no runner service,
  no org config) but has no matrix or marketplace.

---

url: /bupha/getting-started.md
---
# Getting started

bupha ships as tamias packages — the fleet bundles are `type:
bupha` content packs and the `bupha` command itself is a `bins[]`
shim pack (`libraries/bupha` → `tamias-driver-bupha cli` → the
engine lib; there is no cargo-installed binary, T-012). The
product surface is `tamias install`/`deploy` plus `tamias driver
exec <bundle> health|status|logs|hooks`; the watcher engine runs
inside the provider unit via `tamias-driver-bupha host`.

Pick by what you need to do.

* **Tutorials** (learn): [first-run](tutorials/first-run.md)
* **How-to** (tasks): [tamias bundles](how-to/tamias-bundles.md) ·
  [multi-repo](how-to/multi-repo.md) ·
  [shell runner](how-to/shell-runner.md) ·
  [gha runner — your own GHA workflows](how-to/gha-runner.md) ·
  [self-hosted GHA runner](how-to/self-hosted-runner.md) ·
  [distributed runners](how-to/distributed-runners.md) ·
  [sccache backend](how-to/sccache-backend.md)
* **Reference** (lookup): [cli — dev harness](reference/cli.md) ·
  [config](reference/config.md) ·
  [crate api](reference/crate-api.md)
* **Explanation** (why): [architecture](explanation/architecture.md) ·
  [release model](explanation/release-model.md) ·
  [comparison](comparison.md) — vs GHA/hosted CI ·
  [crate scope audit](explanation/crate-scope-audit.md)

Project: [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/9aia/bupha/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ·
[SECURITY](https://github.com/9aia/bupha/blob/main/SECURITY.md) ·
[project](https://github.com/9aia/bupha/blob/main/project/index.md) — TODO, backlog, ADRs
